tabs.title: Entorno existente
tabs.html:
Existing Environment. Fabric Environment

Litware has a Fabric workspace named Workspace1. High concurrency is enabled for Workspace1.

The company has a data engineering team that uses Python for data processing.

Existing Environment. Data Processing

The retail bookstores send sales data at the end of each business day, while the online bookstore constantly provides logs and sales data to a central enterprise resource planning (ERP) system.

Litware implements a medallion architecture by using the following three layers: bronze, silver, and gold. The sales data is ingested from the ERP system as Parquet files that land in the Files folder in a lakehouse. Notebooks are used to transform the files in a Delta table for the bronze and silver layers. The gold layer is in a warehouse that has V-Order disabled.

Litware has image files of book covers in Azure Blob Storage. The files are loaded into the Files folder.

Existing Environment. Sales Data

Month-end sales data is processed on the first calendar day of each month.

Data that is older than one month never changes.

In the source system, the sales data refreshes every six hours starting at midnight each day.

The sales data is captured in a Dataflow Gen1 dataflow. When the dataflow runs, new and historical data is captured. The dataflow captures the following fields of the source:

Sales Date -

Author -

Price -

Units -

SKU -

A table named AuthorSales stores the sales data that relates to each author.

The table contains a column named AuthorEmail. Authors authenticate to a guest Fabric tenant by using their email address.

Existing Environment. Security Groups

Litware has the following security groups:

Sales -

Fabric Admins -

Streaming Admins -

Existing Environment. Performance Issues

Business users perform ad-hoc queries against the warehouse. The business users indicate that reports against the warehouse sometimes run for two hours and fail to load as expected. Upon further investigation, the data engineering team receives the following error message when the reports fail to load: “The SQL query failed while running.”

The data engineering team wants to debug the issue and find queries that cause more than one failure.

When the authors have new book releases, there is often an increase in sales activity. This increase slows the data ingestion process.

The company’s sales team reports that during the last month, the sales data has NOT been up-to-date when they arrive at work in the morning.

tabs.title: Requisitos
tabs.html:
Requirements. Planned Changes

Litware recently signed a contract to receive book reviews. The provider of the reviews exposes the data in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)

buckets.

Litware plans to manage Search Engine Optimization (SEO) for the authors. The SEO data will be streamed from a REST API.

Requirements. Version Control

Litware plans to implement a version control solution in Fabric that will use GitHub integration and follow the principle of least privilege.

Requirements. Governance Requirements

To control data platform costs, the data platform must use only Fabric services and items. Additional Azure resources must NOT be provisioned.

Requirements. Data Requirements

Litware identifies the following data requirements:

Process the SEO data in near-real-time (NRT).

Make the book reviews available in the lakehouse without making a copy of the data.

When a new book cover image arrives in the Files folder, process the image as soon as possible.

tabs.title: Resumen
tabs.html:
Overview

Litware, Inc. is a publishing company that has an online bookstore and several retail bookstores worldwide. Litware also manages an online advertising business for the authors it represents.

tabs.title: Resumen
tabs.html:
Overview. Company Overview

Contoso, Ltd. is an online retail company that wants to modernize its analytics platform by moving to Fabric. The company plans to begin using Fabric for marketing analytics.

Overview. IT Structure

The company’s IT department has a team of data analysts and a team of data engineers that use analytics systems.

The data engineers perform the ingestion, transformation, and loading of data. They prefer to use Python or SQL to transform the data.

The data analysts query data and create semantic models and reports. They are qualified to write queries in Power Query and T-SQL.

tabs.title: Entorno existente
tabs.html:
Existing Environment. Fabric

Contoso has an F64 capacity named Cap1. All Fabric users are allowed to create items.

Contoso has two workspaces named WorkspaceA and WorkspaceB that currently use Pro license mode.

Existing Environment. Source Systems

Contoso has a point of sale (POS) system named POS1 that uses an instance of SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines in the same Microsoft Entra tenant as Fabric. The host virtual machine is on a private virtual network that has public access blocked. POS1 contains all the sales transactions that were processed on the company’s website.

The company has a software as a service (SaaS) online marketing app named MAR1. MAR1 has seven entities. The entities contain data that relates to email open rates and interaction rates, as well as website interactions. The data can be exported from MAR1 by calling REST APIs. Each entity has a different endpoint.

Contoso has been using MAR1 for one year. Data from prior years is stored in Parquet files in an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket. There

are 12 files that range in size from 300 MB to 900 MB and relate to email interactions.

Existing Environment. Product Data

POS1 contains a product list and related data. The data comes from the following three tables:

Products -

ProductCategories -

ProductSubcategories -

In the data, products are related to product subcategories, and subcategories are related to product categories.

Existing Environment. Azure

Contoso has a Microsoft Entra tenant that has the following mail-enabled security groups:

DataAnalysts: Contains the data analysts

DataEngineers: Contains the data engineers

Contoso has an Azure subscription.

The company has an existing Azure DevOps organization and creates a new project for repositories that relate to Fabric.

tabs.title: Problemas
tabs.html:
Existing Environment. User Problems

The VP of marketing at Contoso requires analysis on the effectiveness of different types of email content. It typically takes a week to manually compile and analyze the data. Contoso wants to reduce the time to less than one day by using Fabric.

The data engineering team has successfully exported data from MAR1. The team experiences transient connectivity errors, which causes the data exports to fail.

tabs.title: Requisitos
tabs.html:
Requirements. Planned Changes

Contoso plans to create the following two lakehouses:

Lakehouse1: Will store both raw and cleansed data from the sources Lakehouse2: Will serve data in a dimensional model to users for analytical queries

Additional items will be added to facilitate data ingestion and transformation. Contoso plans to use Azure Repos for source control in Fabric.

Requirements. Technical Requirements

The new lakehouses must follow a medallion architecture by using the following three layers: bronze, silver, and gold. There will be extensive data cleansing required to populate the MAR1 data in the silver layer, including deduplication, the handling of missing values, and the standardizing of capitalization.

Each layer must be fully populated before moving on to the next layer. If any step in populating the lakehouses fails, an email must be sent to the data engineers.

Data imports must run simultaneously, when possible.

The use of email data from the Amazon S3 bucket must meet the following requirements:

Minimize egress costs associated with cross-cloud data access.

Prevent saving a copy of the raw data in the lakehouses.

Items that relate to data ingestion must meet the following requirements:

The items must be source controlled alongside other workspace items.

Ingested data must land in the bronze layer of Lakehouse1 in the Delta format.

No changes other than changes to the file formats must be implemented before the data lands in the bronze layer.

Development effort must be minimized and a built-in connection must be used to import the source data.

In the event of a connectivity error, the ingestion processes must attempt the connection again.

Lakehouses, data pipelines, and notebooks must be stored in WorkspaceA.

Semantic models, reports, and dataflows must be stored in WorkspaceB.

Once a week, old files that are no longer referenced by a Delta table log must be removed.

Requirements. Data Transformation

In the POS1 product data, ProductID values are unique. The product dimension in the gold layer must include only active products from product list. Active products are identified by an IsActive value of 1.

Some product categories and subcategories are NOT assigned to any product.

They are NOT analytically relevant and must be omitted from the product dimension in the gold layer.

Requirements. Data Security

Security in Fabric must meet the following requirements:

The data engineers must have read and write access to all the lakehouses, including the underlying files.

The data analysts must only have read access to the Delta tables in the gold layer.

The data analysts must NOT have access to the data in the bronze and silver layers.

The data engineers must be able to commit changes to source control in WorkspaceA.

q001.stem:
You need to ensure that the data analysts can access the gold layer lakehouse.

What should you do?
options: Add the DataAnalyst group to the Viewer role for WorkspaceA.
Share the lakehouse with the DataAnalysts group and grant the Build reports on the default semantic model permission.
Share the lakehouse with the DataAnalysts group and grant the Read all SQL Endpoint data permission.
Share the lakehouse with the DataAnalysts group and grant the Read all Apache Spark permission.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Share the lakehouse with the DataAnalysts group and grant the Read all SQL Endpoint data permission.

Why it is correct: The case study sets two key security requirements for the data analysts:

  1. They must NOT have access to the bronze and silver layers (Lakehouse1, which is in WorkspaceA).

  2. They must have read-only access to the Delta tables in the gold layer (Lakehouse2, which is also in WorkspaceA). The analyst profile also says they use T-SQL.

Sharing the lakehouse item itself (Lakehouse2) lets you grant item-level access without exposing the other items in the workspace (WorkspaceA). By selecting the "Read all SQL endpoint data" permission during the sharing process, you explicitly enable them to connect and run read-only T-SQL queries directly against the Delta tables of that lakehouse.

  • Official documentation: Share a lakehouse and manage permissions - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Add the DataAnalyst group to the Viewer role for WorkspaceA.

Why it is incorrect: Workspace roles apply to all the items in the workspace. If you assign the Viewer role to the group in WorkspaceA, the data analysts get read access to both lakehouses (Lakehouse1 and Lakehouse2). This directly violates the security requirement that explicitly forbids analysts from accessing the bronze and silver layer data.

  • Official documentation: Roles in workspaces - Microsoft Fabric

B. Share the lakehouse with the DataAnalysts group and grant the Build reports on the default semantic model permission.

Why it is incorrect: Sharing the item individually is the right strategy to isolate access, but the permission to build reports on the default semantic model only lets users create Power BI reports based on that model. It does not give them direct read access to query the underlying Delta tables with T-SQL, which is one of the skills the analysts need according to the case study.

  • Official documentation: Semantic model permissions and sharing - Microsoft Fabric / Share a lakehouse

D. Share the lakehouse with the DataAnalysts group and grant the Read all Apache Spark permission.

Why it is incorrect: The "Read all Apache Spark" permission lets users read the underlying files through Spark code in notebooks. The case study says the data engineers use Python or SQL, but the data analysts use Power Query and T-SQL. To consume the gold layer data through T-SQL queries, the permission they need is the SQL endpoint one, not access through the Spark compute engine.

  • Official documentation: Lakehouse sharing permission details (Read All Apache Spark vs Read All SQL Endpoint) - Microsoft Fabric

q002.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace.

You have semi-structured data.

You need to read the data by using T-SQL, KQL, and Apache Spark. The data will only be written by using Spark.

What should you use to store the data?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: A lakehouse

Why it is correct: In Microsoft Fabric, a lakehouse is ideal for storing structured, unstructured and semi-structured data. The key to this question is the requirement: "The data will only be written by using Spark". When you create a lakehouse in Fabric, the system automatically provisions a SQL analytics endpoint that is strictly read-only. This enforces exactly the design pattern the question asks for: data engineers use Apache Spark to write and transform the data in Delta tables, while consumers can read that same data by using T-SQL (through the SQL endpoint), KQL (through shortcuts or cross-queries) and Spark itself, guaranteeing that the SQL engine does not modify it.

  • Official documentation: What is a lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric? and, above all, the read/write confirmation in SQL analytics endpoint of the lakehouse (read-only).
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

B. An eventhouse

Why it is incorrect: Although an eventhouse (which contains KQL databases) is excellent for analyzing semi-structured data and can be queried with KQL, T-SQL and Apache Spark, it does not meet the premise that writes are done only with Spark. Eventhouses are designed mainly for ingesting telemetry and real-time (streaming) data, so they are usually written to by using eventstreams, native KQL ingestion or IoT connectors, not exclusively through Spark.

  • Official documentation: What is an eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric?

C. A datamart

Why it is incorrect: A datamart in the Fabric/Power BI ecosystem is a self-service relational database solution for business users. It is intended for structured (relational) data, and data is written or ingested through dataflows (Power Query / Dataflow Gen2) or T-SQL, not through Apache Spark engines. It is also not the native solution for handling raw semi-structured data.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to datamarts

D. A warehouse

Why it is incorrect: A data warehouse in Fabric is oriented to structured data. The main difference between a warehouse and a lakehouse in Fabric is the write engine: the warehouse supports full write operations (DML and DDL) by using T-SQL (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE). Since the question requires that writes be done exclusively with Spark, the warehouse is incorrect because it allows active writes through the SQL engine.

  • Official documentation: For a clear view of the read/write difference, see: Compare the capabilities of a warehouse and a lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric.

q003.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a warehouse named Warehouse1.

You have an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server database named Database1 that is accessed by using an on-premises data gateway.

You need to copy data from Database1 to Warehouse1.

Which item should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: A data pipeline

Why it is correct: Data pipelines in Microsoft Fabric, specifically through the Copy data activity, are designed to ingest data at scale. One of their key features is full support for the on-premises data gateway. This lets you establish a secure connection to your on-premises SQL Server database and define the Fabric data warehouse as the destination (sink) of that copy.

  • Official documentation: Access on-premises data sources in Data Factory - Microsoft Fabric and Create a data pipeline to copy data (on-premises source support).
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. A Dataflow Gen1 dataflow

Why it is incorrect: Although Gen1 dataflows (from Power BI) can use the on-premises data gateway, they do not support native writes to a Fabric warehouse. Dataflows Gen1 store their results in Power BI's internal managed storage. To write to a Fabric destination (such as a warehouse, lakehouse or Azure SQL), you would need to use a Dataflow Gen2, not a Gen1.

  • Official documentation: Differences between Dataflow Gen1 and Dataflow Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric (see the "Supported data destinations" section)

C. A KQL queryset

Why it is incorrect: A KQL queryset is an analytical tool designed to run queries over telemetry and time-series data stored in KQL databases (eventhouse) by using the Kusto language. It is not an orchestration, ingestion or data copy tool, and certainly not for moving data from an on-premises SQL Server to a warehouse.

  • Official documentation: What is a KQL queryset? - Microsoft Fabric

D. A notebook

Why it is incorrect: Notebooks in Fabric use Apache Spark. Spark clusters in Fabric are not compatible with the standard on-premises data gateway mentioned in the question. For a Spark notebook to access on-premises data, a much more advanced network setup is required, using a virtual network (VNet) data gateway or a private endpoint. Since the question specifies the use of the on-premises gateway, the notebook is not a viable option.

  • Official documentation: Virtual network data gateways overview (clarifies that Spark workloads and network routing need a VNet, not the standard gateway)

q004.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a warehouse named Warehouse1.

You have an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server database named Database1 that is accessed by using an on-premises data gateway.

You need to copy data from Database1 to Warehouse1.

Which item should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: A data pipeline

Why it is correct: As in the previous question, a data pipeline (through the Copy data activity) is the right tool because it natively supports connecting through the on-premises data gateway to reach an on-premises SQL Server. It also lets you define a Fabric warehouse as the destination of the extracted data, performing batch loads efficiently.

  • Official documentation: Access on-premises data sources in data pipelines - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. An Apache Spark job definition

Why it is incorrect: Spark job definitions run scripts or compiled code on Apache Spark clusters. In Microsoft Fabric, Spark engines cannot use the standard on-premises data gateway to reach on-premises resources. For Spark to access on-premises databases, you need to set up a virtual network and use a virtual network (VNet) data gateway, which is not the resource mentioned in the scenario.

  • Official documentation: Virtual network data gateways and Spark support - Microsoft Fabric

C. A Dataflow Gen1 dataflow

Why it is incorrect: Gen1 dataflows can connect to on-premises sources through the gateway, but they do not support output data destinations. This means a Dataflow Gen1 can only store the data in Power BI's internal storage, but it cannot write or export the data directly to the Fabric warehouse. To write to a warehouse, you would need a Dataflow Gen2.

  • Official documentation: Compare Dataflow Gen1 and Gen2 (Supported data destinations section) - Microsoft Fabric

D. An eventstream

Why it is incorrect: An eventstream is the core item of Real-Time Intelligence in Fabric. It is designed to capture, transform and route high-volume streaming data in real time (such as IoT sensors, Apache Kafka or Azure Event Hubs). It is not designed for batch copy tasks from traditional relational databases such as an on-premises SQL Server.

  • Official documentation: What is Microsoft Fabric Eventstreams?

q005.stem:
You need to implement the solution for the book reviews.

Which should you do?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Create a shortcut

Why it is correct: The case study sets a very specific technical requirement for the book reviews: "Make the book reviews available in the lakehouse without making a copy of the data". It also tells us the data lives in an external Amazon S3 bucket. In Microsoft Fabric, OneLake shortcuts are objects that point to existing storage locations (such as Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, Amazon S3 or Google Cloud Storage) without duplicating or moving the information. When you create an Amazon S3 shortcut in your lakehouse, the data appears and can be queried as if it were local to Fabric, meeting the zero-copy requirement exactly.

  • Official documentation: OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Create a Dataflow Gen2 dataflow

Why it is incorrect: A dataflow (Dataflow Gen2) is used to extract, transform and load (ETL) data. Its main function involves reading the data from the source, processing it and writing a physical copy of that data to a destination (such as a lakehouse or warehouse). Using this tool would directly violate the requirement not to make a copy of the data.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to Dataflows Gen2 - Microsoft Fabric

C. Enable external data sharing

Why it is incorrect: The external data sharing feature in Fabric is designed for the opposite scenario: it lets Litware share its own OneLake data with external users or other Fabric or Azure tenants. It is not a tool designed to mount or read data from an external provider hosted in Amazon S3 into your own Fabric environment.

  • Official documentation: External data sharing overview - Microsoft Fabric

D. Create a data pipeline

Why it is incorrect: Data pipelines are used to orchestrate workflows and ingest large volumes of data, usually through the Copy data activity. As with Dataflow Gen2, a pipeline would perform a physical copy and a network transfer to bring the data from Amazon S3 into the Fabric lakehouse storage, violating the business requirement not to duplicate the information.

  • Official documentation: Data pipeline concepts - Microsoft Fabric

q006.stem:
You need to resolve the sales data issue. The solution must minimize the amount of data transferred.

What should you do?
options: Spilt the dataflow into two dataflows.
Configure scheduled refresh for the dataflow.
Configure incremental refresh for the dataflow. Set Store rows from the past to 1 Month.
Configure incremental refresh for the dataflow. Set Refresh rows from the past to 1 Year.
Configure incremental refresh for the dataflow. Set Refresh rows from the past to 1 Month.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: Configure incremental refresh for the dataflow. Set the refresh rows from the past to 1 month.

Why it is correct: The main problem reported by the sales team is that the data takes too long to load ("it has not been updated by the time they arrive at work in the morning"), which is made worse because "new and historical data are captured" on every run (full refresh). The requirement is to minimize the amount of data transferred.
Incremental refresh is the native solution for this. Its configuration has two key parameters:

  1. Store rows from the past: Defines how much total history is kept.

  2. Refresh rows from the past: Defines which time window of data is queried from the source system on each run.

The case study explicitly says: "The month-end sales data is processed on the first calendar day of each month. Data older than one month never changes." Therefore, setting the refresh window to 1 month ensures that the dataflow only requests from the source the transactions of the last 30/31 days (the only ones that can change or be newly inserted), leaving the rest of the history untouched. This minimizes network data transfer, dramatically speeds up the process and ensures the data is ready in the morning.

  • Official documentation: Use incremental refresh in dataflows ("Refresh rows from the past" section) - Microsoft Fabric / Power Query
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Split the dataflow into two dataflows.

Why it is incorrect: Although separating dataflows into extraction (staging) and transformation dataflows is a good architecture practice, if both still do a full load from the source, the amount of data transferred from the ERP will not be minimized and the read time from the source will remain a bottleneck.

  • Official documentation: Best practices for designing and developing complex dataflows (it talks about separation, but does not replace the need for incremental refresh)

B. Configure scheduled refresh for the dataflow.

Why it is incorrect: Setting up a scheduled refresh automates when the dataflow runs (for example, at midnight), but it does not change how the data is extracted. If incremental refresh is not configured, the scheduled refresh will keep doing a massive extraction of the entire history, so the process will remain too slow.

  • Official documentation: Data refresh in Power BI and Fabric (explains that a full refresh consumes a lot of memory and time)

C. Configure incremental refresh for the dataflow. Configure store rows from the past to 1 month.

Why it is incorrect: The "store rows from the past" parameter dictates how much historical data the destination keeps. If you set this to 1 month, you would be purging and deleting from the dataflow all of the company's sales history older than 30 days, causing a critical loss of historical data.

  • Official documentation: Use incremental refresh in dataflows ("Store rows from the past" section warns about time-based retention)

D. Configure incremental refresh for the dataflow. Configure refresh rows from the past to 1 year.

Why it is incorrect: Although using incremental refresh is the right path, setting the refresh window ("Refresh rows") to 1 year means that every night 365 days of data will be queried again and overwritten. Since the case says data older than one month never changes, you would be transferring 11 months of redundant data over the network every day. This violates the requirement to "minimize the amount of data transferred".

  • Official documentation: Use incremental refresh (same reference, focusing on the optimal refresh window setting based on business rules)

q007.stem:
HOTSPOT -

You need to recommend a method to populate the POS1 data to the lakehouse medallion layers.

What should you recommend for each layer? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Bronze layer: A pipeline Copy activity

  • Silver layer: A notebook

Detailed analysis for the Bronze layer

Why "A pipeline Copy activity" is correct: The case study sets several strict requirements for the initial ingestion into the bronze layer:

  • "No changes other than file format changes should be implemented before the data lands in the bronze layer": The Copy activity is designed exactly for moving raw data, letting you change the source format (such as SQL) to the destination format (Delta Parquet) without applying complex transformations.

  • "Development effort must be minimized... ": The Copy activity is a visual (no-code) interface that requires minimal development effort.

  • "In the event of a connectivity error, the ingestion processes must retry the connection": Data pipeline activities in Fabric have built-in native support for retry policies, which lets you automatically configure how many times and at what interval the connection should be retried in case of transient failures.

  • Official documentation: Copy activity in data pipelines (support for retries and Delta format) - Microsoft Fabric

Why the other options are incorrect for the bronze layer:

A notebook: Although it can ingest data, it requires writing custom code to implement retry logic for connectivity failures, which violates the requirement to "minimize development effort".

  • Official documentation: Author and run Apache Spark notebooks - Microsoft Fabric

A Dataflow Gen2 dataflow: Dataflows Gen2 are transformation-oriented (Power Query). Using them only to copy data without transforming it adds unnecessary overhead, and their native integration with automatic retry policies at the network level is not as direct as in the Copy activity.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to Dataflows Gen2 - Microsoft Fabric

A pipeline stored procedure: A stored procedure runs inside a SQL database engine. It cannot be used to extract data from an external source and write it as Delta files in a lakehouse.

  • Official documentation: Stored procedure activity in pipelines - Microsoft Fabric

Detailed analysis for the Silver layer

Why "A notebook" is correct: To move from the bronze layer to the silver layer, the case requires:

  • "Extensive data cleansing will be required... including deduplication, handling of missing values, and standardization of capitalization".

  • "Data engineers perform the ingestion, transformation, and load... They prefer to use Python or SQL to transform the data". Notebooks in Fabric use Apache Spark (PySpark/Spark SQL), which fits the engineering team's preference (Python or SQL) perfectly. In addition, Spark DataFrames are ideal and highly efficient for performing advanced cleansing at scale (deduplication with .dropDuplicates(), null handling with .fillna(), and string standardization).

  • Official documentation: Transform data with Apache Spark notebooks - Microsoft Fabric

Why the other options are incorrect for the silver layer:

A Dataflow Gen2 dataflow: Although Dataflows Gen2 (Power Query) are excellent for cleaning data, the case specifies that the data engineers are the ones who perform this task and they prefer to use Python or SQL, not Power Query (M). The data analysts are the ones who use Power Query, but the ETL is done by the engineers.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to Dataflows Gen2 (Using Power Query) - Microsoft Fabric

A pipeline Copy activity: It does not allow data transformations (such as deduplication or null handling).

A pipeline stored procedure: The Delta tables of the bronze/silver layers in a lakehouse do not support running stored procedures to transform them natively (stored procedures are more typical of a pure relational warehouse environment).

q008.stem:
HOTSPOT -

You need to troubleshoot the ad-hoc query issue.

How should you complete the statement? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Drop-down 1: queryinsights.frequently_run_queries

  • Drop-down 2: number_of_failed_runs > 1

Detailed analysis for the Correct Options

Drop-down 1: queryinsights.frequently_run_queries Why it is correct: To meet the goal of "finding queries that cause more than one failure", you must query a system view that aggregates the execution history and calculates statistical metrics for each individual query over time. The queryinsights.frequently_run_queries view in the Fabric warehouse is designed exactly for this purpose. Reviewing its official schema confirms that this view natively contains the pre-calculated columns required in the SELECT and WHERE blocks of the image: last_run_start_time, last_run_command, last_run_total_elapsed_time_ms and the error count metrics needed for the second condition.

  • Official documentation: queryinsights.frequently_run_queries (Transact-SQL) - Microsoft Learn

Drop-down 2: number_of_failed_runs > 1 Why it is correct: The case study sets an explicit, literal technical requirement: the team needs to "find queries that cause more than one failure". The number_of_failed_runs column belongs to the schema of the view selected in the previous step and acts as a historical error counter for each query. Filtering by > 1 translates this business rule directly into T-SQL.

  • Official documentation: Monitoring using Query Insights in Fabric (Query Insights) - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Incorrect options for Drop-down 1 (the source view):

Options: queryinsights.exec_requests_history / queryinsights.exec_sessions_history Why they are incorrect: These two views act as a raw transactional log (storing a separate row each time a request is run or a session is opened over time). Because they do not group or summarize queries, they contain no aggregated columns starting with number_of_... (such as the total failure count of a query) and have no last_run_... prefixes (because each row is a run). If you put either of these two views in the FROM clause, the SQL query will return a syntax error for nonexistent columns.

  • Official documentation: queryinsights.exec_requests_history (Transact-SQL) - Microsoft Learn

Option: queryinsights.long_running_queries Why it is incorrect: Although this view shares an almost identical schema with the frequently run queries view and also includes columns with aggregated metrics, the Fabric engine optimizes and orders it to strictly return queries based on historical execution time (the slowest ones). When the goal is to isolate a pattern of recurring failures and error frequency ("more than one failure"), the official architecture dictates using the frequently_run_queries view to ensure that the problematic query is found in the statistical result set.

  • Official documentation: Identifying bottlenecks using queryinsights - Microsoft Learn

Incorrect options for Drop-down 2 (the filter condition):

Options: number_of_canceled_runs > 1 / number_of_runs > 1 Why they are incorrect: Neither of them isolates the system error mentioned in the case study ("The SQL query failed"). number_of_canceled_runs would filter queries that were aborted or manually canceled by a user or administrator before finishing, which is not a technical failure. On the other hand, number_of_runs > 1 would simply filter queries that have been run multiple times over time, regardless of whether they fully succeeded or failed.

  • Official documentation: frequently_run_queries columns and metrics - Microsoft Learn

Options: max_run_total_elapsed_time_ms > 7200000 / median_total_elapsed_time_ms > 7200000 Why they are incorrect: The first logical filter of the WHERE clause that is already written in the image bounds the extreme-duration problem (last_run_total_elapsed_time_ms > 7200000, equivalent to the reports that "sometimes take two hours" mentioned by the business users). The AND operator of this second drop-down is intended exclusively to resolve the second condition of the requirement ("that cause more than one failure"). Adding another execution time metric would be redundant and would ruin the error search logic.

  • Official documentation: Transact-SQL logical operators (AND) - Microsoft Learn

q009.stem:
You need to schedule the population of the medallion layers to meet the technical requirements.

What should you do?
options: Schedule a data pipeline that calls other data pipelines.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Schedule a data pipeline that calls other data pipelines.

Detailed analysis for the Correct Option

Why "Schedule a data pipeline that calls other data pipelines." is correct: The case study sets several critical orchestration requirements that can only be solved efficiently by using a "master pipeline" pattern that invokes other (child) pipelines:

  1. "Each layer must be fully populated before moving on to the next": A main data pipeline can use the Invoke pipeline activity to run the processes sequentially. It first calls the bronze layer pipeline, waits natively for it to finish successfully, and only then invokes the silver layer one.

  2. "If any step in the lakehouse population fails, an email must be sent to the data engineers": Data pipelines in Fabric let you configure conditional control flow paths (the "On fail" path) that can directly trigger the Office 365 Outlook activity to send the alert email, meeting the requirement to "minimize development effort" without having to write complex code.

  3. "Data imports must run simultaneously, when possible": Within the specific ingestion pipelines, multiple Copy activities can be placed in parallel.

  • Official documentation: Invoke pipeline activity in Data Factory - Microsoft Fabric and Control flow in data pipelines (success/failure paths) - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Why the other options are incorrect:

B Schedule a notebook: Although a notebook can run and orchestrate Python/PySpark code, setting up an email alerting system for failures and handling simultaneous ingestion would require developing and maintaining custom code with external libraries. This directly violates the requirement that "Development effort must be minimized".

  • Official documentation: Author and run Apache Spark notebooks - Microsoft Fabric

C Schedule an Apache Spark job: Apache Spark job definitions are designed to run batch scripts in isolation. They have no native or visual interface to manage dependencies between layers, control the success/failure flow, or send email notifications in an integrated way.

  • Official documentation: What is an Apache Spark job definition? - Microsoft Fabric

D Schedule multiple data pipelines: If you schedule multiple pipelines independently (for example, based on separate schedules), it is impossible to guarantee the strict requirement that "Each layer must be fully populated before moving on to the next". If the bronze layer ingestion is delayed, the silver layer could start running prematurely, processing incomplete data or failing.

  • Official documentation: Pipeline runs and triggers in Data Factory - Microsoft Fabric

q010.stem:
DRAG DROP -

You have a Fabric eventhouse that contains a KQL database. The database contains a table named TaxiData. The following is a sample of the data in TaxiData.

You need to build two KQL queries. The solution must meet the following requirements:

One of the queries must partition RunningTotalAmount by VendorID.

The other query must create a column named FirstPickupDateTime that shows the first value of each hour from tpep_pickup_datetime partitioned by payment_type.

How should you complete each query? To answer, drag the appropriate values the correct targets. Each value may be used once, more than once, or not at all. You may need to drag the split bar between panes or scroll to view content.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Statement1: row_cumsum

  • Statement2: row_window_session

Detailed analysis for Statement1

Why "row_cumsum" is correct: The first requirement asks for a cumulative sum (RunningTotalAmount) partitioned by VendorID. In Kusto Query Language (KQL), the row_cumsum() function is used to calculate the cumulative sum of a column over a serialized set of rows. By providing the second argument VendorID != prev(VendorID), you tell the function to restart the cumulative sum every time the VendorID value changes compared to the previous row, achieving exactly the requested partitioning effect.

  • Official documentation: row_cumsum() function in KQL - Microsoft Learn

Why the other options are incorrect for Statement1:

row_window_session: This function is used to calculate the start of time-based session windows, not to perform cumulative mathematical sums of monetary amounts.

  • Official documentation: row_window_session() function in KQL - Microsoft Learn

row_rank_dense: It calculates the dense rank of the current row, returning positions (1, 2, 2, 3...), not cumulative sums of a metric such as total_amount.

  • Official documentation: row_rank_dense() function in KQL - Microsoft Learn

row_rank_min: It calculates the minimum rank (standard rank) of the current row, which would return a ranking with gaps (1, 2, 2, 4...), which does not meet the requirement of calculating a running or cumulative total.

  • Official documentation: row_rank_min() function in KQL - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis for Statement2

Why "row_window_session" is correct: The second requirement asks for a column that shows the "first value of each hour" (time window) of the date/time column, partitioned by payment_type. The row_window_session() function is designed specifically to calculate session start values over a serialized set. Its arguments in the code (tpep_pickup_datetime, 1h, 0m, payment_type != prev(payment_type)) perfectly define the time column, the maximum session window (1 hour), the maximum time between events (0 minutes, indicating strict hourly jumps) and the restart condition (partition) when the payment method changes.

  • Official documentation: row_window_session() function in KQL - Microsoft Learn

Why the other options are incorrect for Statement2:

row_cumsum: It cumulatively adds numeric values. It cannot be used to evaluate time intervals or to return session start timestamps.

  • Official documentation: row_cumsum() function in KQL - Microsoft Learn

row_rank_dense: It assigns a ranking number to rows. The requirement asks for a date/time (DateTime) value corresponding to the first value of the hour, not a sequential position number.

  • Official documentation: row_rank_dense() function in KQL - Microsoft Learn

row_rank_min: Like the previous one, it returns the ranking number based on the minimum value; it does not manage or group date/time values into logical windows nor return the starting timestamp.

  • Official documentation: row_rank_min() function in KQL - Microsoft Learn

q011.stem:
You have a Fabric F32 capacity that contains a workspace. The workspace contains a warehouse named DW1 that is modelled by using MD5 hash surrogate keys.

DW1 contains a single fact table that has grown from 200 million rows to 500 million rows during the past year.

You have Microsoft Power BI reports that are based on Direct Lake. The reports show year-over-year values.

Users report that the performance of some of the reports has degraded over time and some visuals show errors.

You need to resolve the performance issues. The solution must meet the following requirements:

Provide the best query performance.

Minimize operational costs.

Which should you do?
options: Change the MD5 hash to SHA256.
Modify the surrogate keys to use a different data type.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Increase the capacity.

Detailed analysis for the Correct Option

Option: Increase the capacity.

  • Why it is correct: In Microsoft Fabric Direct Lake mode, data is loaded directly from the Delta Parquet files into the RAM of the assigned capacity so that the Power BI engine can query it at maximum speed. Each Fabric SKU tier (such as an F32 capacity) has a strict memory limit available for semantic models. When a fact table grows massively from 200 million to 500 million rows, the data volume completely exceeds the RAM quota allowed for an F32 SKU, which causes memory overflow failures, errors in the visuals ("The SQL query failed during execution") and performance degradation. The only valid architectural solution to scale the in-memory resources and accommodate the new data volume is to increase the capacity (scale up to a higher SKU).

  • Official documentation: Direct Lake overview in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option: Enable V-Order

  • Why it is incorrect: Although V-Order is an excellent native columnar storage optimization practice in Fabric that reduces space and improves read speed in Delta Parquet, it cannot solve a problem where the total data size (500 million rows) physically exceeds the maximum RAM limit allowed by the capacity SKU. If the dataset exceeds the available memory, optimizing storage compression will not prevent the overflow failure in Direct Lake.

  • Official documentation: Delta table optimization and V-Order in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option: Change the MD5 hash to SHA256

  • Why it is incorrect: Changing from an MD5 hash to SHA256 generates 256-bit cryptographic keys, which are significantly longer and heavier. This needlessly increases memory and storage consumption, worsening the overall performance of joins and further aggravating the memory saturation problem.

  • Official documentation: Dimensional modeling and performance considerations in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option: Modify the surrogate keys to use a different data type

  • Why it is incorrect: Although adjusting key data types can offer slight space improvements at a small scale, in a massive 500-million-row table the bottleneck is an exceeded infrastructure capacity limit. Modifying the data types will not reduce the memory footprint enough to accommodate the massive growth that exceeded the F32 capacity.

  • Official documentation: Data modeling guidelines for Power BI semantic models - Microsoft Learn

Option: Create views

  • Why it is incorrect: Views or logical query abstraction layers do not change the physical structure of the data nor resolve the RAM limits imposed by the hardware capacity. They will keep failing when trying to load the 500 million rows into the Direct Lake engine.

  • Official documentation: Create and use views in Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse - Microsoft Learn

q012.stem:
HOTSPOT -

You have a Fabric workspace that contains a warehouse named DW1. DW1 contains the following tables and columns.

You need to create an output that presents the summarized values of all the order quantities by year and product. The results must include a summary of the order quantities at the year level for all the products.

How should you complete the code? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • First drop-down (SELECT): SELECT YEAR

  • Second drop-down (GROUP BY): GROUPING SETS ((YEAR(SO.ModifiedDate), P.Name), (YEAR(SO.ModifiedDate)))

Detailed analysis for the First drop-down (SELECT)

Why "SELECT YEAR" is correct: The requirement states that the results must present the summarized data "by year". Since the ModifiedDate column contains the full order date, we need to extract only the year. In T-SQL, the YEAR(date) function is used for exactly this purpose. By placing SELECT YEAR before the parenthesis (SO.ModifiedDate), the resulting syntax is SELECT YEAR(SO.ModifiedDate) AS OrderDate, which is perfectly valid and extracts the year correctly.

  • Official documentation: YEAR function (Transact-SQL) - Microsoft Learn

Why the other options are incorrect for the First drop-down:

SELECT CAST: The CAST function is used to convert one data type into another, but its syntax requires explicitly specifying the target data type inside the parentheses (for example, CAST(SO.ModifiedDate AS INT)). The code provided in the image does not contain the AS [data_type] clause, so it would cause a syntax error.

  • Official documentation: CAST and CONVERT functions (Transact-SQL) - Microsoft Learn

SELECT CONVERT: Like CAST, CONVERT requires specifying the target data type, and its standard syntax requires the data type to be the first argument (for example, CONVERT(INT, SO.ModifiedDate)). The code fragment provided does not meet this structure, resulting in an error.

  • Official documentation: CAST and CONVERT functions (Transact-SQL) - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis for the Second drop-down (GROUP BY)

Why "GROUPING SETS ((YEAR(SO.ModifiedDate), P.Name), (YEAR(SO.ModifiedDate)))" is correct: The scenario requires two specific levels of grouping:

  1. Summarized values by year and product: (YEAR(SO.ModifiedDate), P.Name).

  2. A yearly-level summary for all products: (YEAR(SO.ModifiedDate)) The GROUPING SETS clause in T-SQL lets you explicitly define multiple grouping sets with surgical precision in a single query. This option is the only one that specifies exactly the two groupings required by the question, without adding extra totals that were not requested.

  • Official documentation: GROUP BY (Transact-SQL) - GROUPING SETS - Microsoft Learn

Why the other options are incorrect for the Second drop-down:

CUBE(YEAR(SO.ModifiedDate), P.Name): The CUBE function generates groupings for all possible combinations. It would produce results by (Year, Product), by (Year), by (Product) and a grand total (). It generates aggregations by product ignoring the year and a grand total that were not requested in the requirements.

  • Official documentation: GROUP BY (Transact-SQL) - CUBE - Microsoft Learn

ROLLUP(YEAR(SO.ModifiedDate), P.Name): The ROLLUP function assumes a hierarchy and generates subtotals. It would produce (Year, Product), (Year) and a grand total (). Although it is closer than CUBE, it still computes an absolute grand total row () that the requirement did not expressly ask for, making GROUPING SETS the mathematically exact option for what is requested.

  • Official documentation: GROUP BY (Transact-SQL) - ROLLUP - Microsoft Learn

YEAR(SO.ModifiedDate), P.Name: This is a standard GROUP BY. It would only group by the combination of year and product on each row, but it would omit entirely the requirement to include the "summary of the order quantities at the yearly level for all products" (the subtotal per year).

  • Official documentation: GROUP BY (Transact-SQL) - Basic syntax - Microsoft Learn

q013.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1. Data is ingested into Lakehouse1 as one flat table. The table contains the following columns.

You plan to load the data into a dimensional model and implement a star schema. From the original flat table, you create two tables named FactSales and DimProduct. You will track changes in DimProduct.

You need to prepare the data.

Which three columns should you include in the DimProduct table? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option B: ProductName

  • Option C: ProductColor

  • Option F: ProductID

Detailed analysis for the Correct Options

Why "ProductName", "ProductColor" and "ProductID" are correct: In dimensional modeling (star schema), dimension tables (DimProduct) are used to store entities and their descriptive attributes that give context to the business data, answering the question of "what" is being sold. To correctly build the product dimension from the original flat table:

ProductID (F): It is the unique identifier of the product (business key), strictly necessary to identify each record in the dimension and to act as the key that will relate this table to the fact table.

ProductName (B) and ProductColor (C): They are the purely descriptive attributes inherent to the product. These are the text fields by which users will filter, group and analyze the data in reports (for example, "total sales by product name and color").

  • Official documentation: Understand star schema and dimension tables - Microsoft Fabric / Power BI
answer.incorrect:
Why the other options are incorrect:

A Date: The transaction date is an attribute of the sales event, not of the physical product itself. In a proper star schema, this field would reside in the fact table (FactSales), acting as a foreign key to connect to a separate date dimension (DimDate).

  • Official documentation: Date dimensions in star schema models - Microsoft Fabric

D TransactionID: It represents the unique identifier of the sales transaction (the ticket or receipt). This defines the grain of the business event that took place and therefore belongs strictly to the fact table (FactSales), not to the dimension that describes the product catalog.

  • Official documentation: Grain in fact tables - Microsoft Fabric

E SalesAmount: It is a quantitative measure (a measurable numeric value) generated by the sales event. In classic dimensional modeling, quantifiable measures are always stored in the fact table (FactSales) so they can be aggregated (summed, averaged, etc.) in reports.

  • Official documentation: Fact tables and measure storage - Microsoft Fabric

q014.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains a notebook named Notebook1.

In Workspace1, you create a new notebook named Notebook2.

You need to ensure that you can attach Notebook2 to the same Apache Spark session as Notebook1.

What should you do?
options: Enable dynamic allocation for the Spark pool.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Enable high concurrency for notebooks.

Detailed analysis for the Correct Option

Why "Enable high concurrency for notebooks" is correct: In Microsoft Fabric, high concurrency is the platform-specific feature designed to let users share a single Apache Spark session across multiple notebooks. When this mode is enabled at the workspace level, when Notebook1 starts a session, Notebook2 can attach to that same active session instantly. This eliminates the cold start time for subsequent notebooks and greatly optimizes the use of compute resources.

  • Official documentation: High concurrency mode in Fabric notebooks - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Why the other options are incorrect:

B Enable dynamic allocation for the Spark pool: Dynamic allocation lets a Spark application scale out by automatically adding or removing executors based on its current workload. However, it does not provide the ability to share a session between several independent notebooks.

  • Official documentation: Dynamic allocation in Spark pools - Microsoft Fabric

C Change the runtime version: The runtime version defines which versions of base software components are installed (such as Spark 3.3, 3.4, Delta Lake, Python, etc.). Upgrading or changing the runtime affects code dependencies, but it in no way enables session sharing between notebooks.

  • Official documentation: Spark runtimes in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Fabric

D Increase the number of executors: (Note: "Albaceas" is a poor automated translation in the exams for the word "Executors" / "Ejecutores"). Increasing the number of executors simply gives a Spark session more parallel processing capacity. A session with more executors will be faster at processing large volumes of data, but it will remain exclusive to the notebook that started it unless high concurrency is enabled.

  • Official documentation: Spark pool properties and node configuration - Microsoft Fabric

q015.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1. Lakehouse1 contains the following tables:

Orders -

Customer -

Employee -

The Employee table contains Personally Identifiable Information (PII).

A data engineer is building a workflow that requires writing data to the Customer table, however, the user does NOT have the elevated permissions required to view the contents of the Employee table.

You need to ensure that the data engineer can write data to the Customer table without reading data from the Employee table.

Which three actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
options: Share Lakehouse1 with the data engineer.
Assign the data engineer the Contributor role for Workspace2.
Assign the data engineer the Viewer role for Workspace2.
Assign the data engineer the Contributor role for Workspace1.
Migrate the Employee table from Lakehouse1 to Lakehouse2.
Create a new workspace named Workspace2 that contains a new lakehouse named Lakehouse2.
Assign the data engineer the Viewer role for Workspace1.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option D: Assign the data engineer the Contributor role for Workspace1.

  • Option E: Migrate the Employee table from Lakehouse1 to Lakehouse2.

  • Option F: Create a new workspace named Workspace2 that contains a new lakehouse named Lakehouse2.

Detailed analysis for the Correct Options

Why "Assign the Contributor role for Workspace1", "Migrate the table" and "Create a new workspace" are correct: In the current Microsoft Fabric security architecture, a lakehouse does not support table-level security (TLS) or object-level security (OLS) to limit write operations through the Apache Spark engine or the file interface. If a user has permissions to write to a lakehouse, they inherently have access to read and write all the tables and files in that lakehouse.
To meet the strict requirement that the engineer can write to the Customer table but NOT see the Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in the Employee table, you must use a physical isolation or workspace isolation pattern:

  1. (Option F) You must create an entirely new workspace (Workspace2) with its own lakehouse (Lakehouse2) to act as a secure vault.

  2. (Option E) You must extract (migrate) the sensitive table (Employee) out of Lakehouse1 and move it to the secure vault (Lakehouse2).

  3. (Option D) Finally, for the data engineer to be able to do their task of writing to the Customer table, you must grant them the Contributor role in Workspace1. As a Contributor, they have the elevated permissions to write to Lakehouse1, but since the PII table no longer resides there, access to the sensitive data is completely blocked.

  • Official documentation: Lakehouse security model and workspace isolation - Microsoft Fabric and Workspace roles (Contributor role write permissions) - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Why the other options are incorrect:

A Share Lakehouse1 with the data engineer: The item-level Share feature is designed mainly to grant read access (Read, Read All SQL Endpoint, Read All Apache Spark). It is not the right method to provide comprehensive write permissions for data engineering workflows. In addition, if the Employee table is not migrated, the engineer would still have access to the PII.

  • Official documentation: Share a lakehouse and manage permissions - Microsoft Fabric

B Assign the data engineer the Contributor role for Workspace2: Workspace2 is the secure environment where the sensitive Employee table will be isolated. Granting any write or management access to this user in Workspace2 would directly violate the requirement that they must NOT be able to see the table.

  • Official documentation: Roles in workspaces - Microsoft Fabric

C Assign the data engineer the Viewer role for Workspace2: As with option B, the Viewer role would grant them read permissions on the SQL analytics endpoint, allowing them to read the PII data in the Employee table. This breaks the main security requirement.

  • Official documentation: Viewer role permissions in workspaces - Microsoft Fabric

G Assign the data engineer the Viewer role for Workspace1: The Viewer role in Fabric is strictly read-only. The scenario explicitly requires the data engineer to build a workflow that "requires writing data to the Customer table". With the Viewer role, any write attempt (INSERT, UPDATE) will fail.

  • Official documentation: Roles in workspaces - Microsoft Fabric

q016.stem:
You have a Fabric warehouse named DW1. DW1 contains a table that stores sales data and is used by multiple sales representatives.

You plan to implement row-level security (RLS).

You need to ensure that the sales representatives can see only their respective data.

Which warehouse object do you require to implement RLS?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: FUNCTION

Detailed analysis for the Correct Option

Why "FUNCTION" is correct: In Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse (and in T-SQL in general), row-level security (RLS) requires creating an inline table-valued function. This function acts as the "access predicate", containing the conditional logic that evaluates whether the current user (usually verified through the system function USER_NAME() or SUSER_SNAME()) has permission to see a specific row. Once the function is created, it is bound to the table through an object called a security policy.

  • Official documentation: Row-level security in Fabric data warehousing - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Why the other options are incorrect:

A STORED PROCEDURE: Stored procedures are used to group and run multiple SQL statements (such as complex ETL tasks, inserts or updates), but the database engine does not allow them to be used as predicates within a security policy. RLS strictly requires a function because it must be evaluated continuously "inline", row by row, during the execution of a SELECT query.

  • Official documentation: Stored procedures in data warehousing - Microsoft Fabric

B CONSTRAINT: Constraints, such as primary keys, foreign keys or check constraints, are used exclusively to guarantee the integrity and validity of the data stored in tables. They are not security objects and cannot evaluate the user context to filter results.

  • Official documentation: Primary, foreign, and unique keys in data warehousing - Microsoft Fabric

C SCHEMA: A schema is a logical container used to group database objects and manage permissions at a higher level (object-level security). Although it is a good design practice to create a dedicated schema (for example, CREATE SCHEMA Security) to hold the RLS function, the schema by itself does not filter data nor contain the row evaluation logic.

  • Official documentation: Database schemas in SQL - Microsoft Learn

q017.stem:
HOTSPOT -

You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1_DEV that contains the following items:

10 reports

Four notebooks -

Three lakehouses -

Two data pipelines -

Two Dataflow Gen1 dataflows -

Three Dataflow Gen2 dataflows -

Five semantic models that each has a scheduled refresh policy You create a deployment pipeline named Pipeline1 to move items from Workspace1_DEV to a new workspace named Workspace1_TEST.

You deploy all the items from Workspace1_DEV to Workspace1_TEST.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true.

Otherwise, select No.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Data from the semantic models will be deployed to the target stage: No

  • The Dataflow Gen1 dataflows will be deployed to the target stage: Yes

  • The scheduled refresh policies will be deployed to the target stage: No

Detailed analysis for the First statement

Why "No" is correct: Deployment pipelines in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI are designed to promote the logic, structure and code, that is, the metadata of the items. When a semantic model is deployed to a new stage (such as from DEV to TEST), the underlying data is not copied or transferred. The semantic model in the target workspace is created only with its structure (schema) and will require you to configure the source credentials and run a refresh in the target environment to be populated with data.

  • Official documentation: Deployment pipelines concepts (Deployments do not include data or credentials) - Microsoft Fabric

Detailed analysis for the Second statement

Why "Yes" is correct: Fabric deployment pipelines support a wide variety of items, explicitly including traditional Power BI dataflows (now called Dataflow Gen1), as well as the new Dataflow Gen2. Since the statement says "You deploy all the objects from Workspace1_DEV to Workspace1_TEST", and since Dataflow Gen1 is an item fully supported by the native Fabric continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) process, these dataflows will be successfully deployed to the target stage.

  • Official documentation: Supported items in Fabric deployment pipelines - Microsoft Fabric

Detailed analysis for the Third statement

Why "No" is correct: In deployment pipelines, certain item properties are considered "environment-specific" and, by design, are not copied or overwritten during a deployment to a target stage. Scheduled refresh settings belong to this group of exclusions. Therefore, even if a semantic model or dataflow is deployed, its refresh schedule configuration will not travel with it; you will have to configure scheduled refresh manually and independently in the TEST environment.

  • Official documentation: Item properties that are not copied in the deployment process - Microsoft Fabric

q018.stem:
You have a Fabric deployment pipeline that uses three workspaces named Dev, Test, and Prod.

You need to deploy an eventhouse as part of the deployment process.

What should you use to add the eventhouse to the deployment process?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: a deployment pipeline

Detailed analysis for the Correct Option

Why "a deployment pipeline" is correct: The scenario describes a classic flow with three workspaces (Dev, Test and Prod) that corresponds exactly to the native Microsoft Fabric deployment pipelines. Eventhouses and KQL databases (part of Real-Time Intelligence) are natively supported as items in Fabric deployment pipelines. Therefore, to add the eventhouse to the code promotion process between environments, you simply use the native deployment pipeline that is already set up, without needing to resort to external tools.

  • Official documentation: Git integration and deployment pipelines (Supported items) - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Why the other options are incorrect:

A GitHub Actions: Although Fabric supports Git (GitHub) integration for source control, using GitHub Actions would mean building a completely external deployment (CI/CD) pipeline using the REST API or CLI. This adds unnecessary complexity given that the question states that a native Fabric deployment pipeline with the three environments already exists, and the eventhouse is fully supported by it.

  • Official documentation: Fabric deployment pipelines overview - Microsoft Fabric

C an Azure DevOps pipeline: Identically to GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines is an external CI/CD orchestration tool. Using Git integration with Azure DevOps is excellent for version control, but for promoting and deploying from one environment to another (Dev -> Test -> Prod) when a Fabric pipeline is already configured, the correct and most efficient approach is to use the native tool (the Fabric deployment pipeline), which already supports eventhouses, rather than building a parallel pipeline in Azure DevOps.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to Git integration and deployment pipelines in Fabric - Microsoft Fabric

q019.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains a warehouse named Warehouse1.

You plan to deploy Warehouse1 to a new workspace named Workspace2.

As part of the deployment process, you need to verify whether Warehouse1 contains invalid references. The solution must minimize development effort.

What should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: a database project

Detailed analysis for the Correct Option

Option: a database project

  • Why it is correct: A SQL database project (SQL Database Project) lets you extract, version and build the schema of a Microsoft Fabric warehouse locally or through CI/CD tools (such as Visual Studio Code). During the build process, the engine performs an exhaustive static analysis of all references between T-SQL objects (tables, views, stored procedures) and automatically detects any unresolved or invalid reference. This meets the requirement to minimize development effort, since it provides detailed build errors without having to write custom code.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to database projects for Microsoft Fabric warehouses - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option: a deployment pipeline

  • Why it is incorrect: Deployment pipelines in Microsoft Fabric are designed for the lifecycle promotion and orchestration of items between workspaces (such as Development, Test and Production) and for applying parameterization rules. However, their purpose is the movement and synchronization of metadata, not performing deep static analysis of T-SQL code or verifying the validity of cross-object references before deploying.

  • Official documentation: Fabric deployment pipelines overview - Microsoft Learn

Option: a Python script

  • Why it is incorrect: Although a Python script could be used to interact with APIs or connect to the database, it would require complex custom development from scratch to analyze the T-SQL structure, parse dependencies and validate schemas. This directly violates the requirement to minimize development effort, since a native tool specific to this purpose exists.

  • Official documentation: Python connectivity to SQL warehouse in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option: a T-SQL script

  • Why it is incorrect: Writing a custom T-SQL script (for example, querying system catalog views such as sys.sql_expression_dependencies) to look for broken references would require the creation, testing and ongoing maintenance of custom manual code. Like the Python script, it breaks the principle of minimizing development effort when a database project resolves static validation automatically and in an integrated way.

  • Official documentation: sys.sql_expression_dependencies (Transact-SQL) - Microsoft Learn

q020.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a Real-Time Intelligence solution and an eventhouse.

Users report that from OneLake file explorer, they cannot see the data from the eventhouse.

You enable OneLake availability for the eventhouse.

What will be copied to OneLake?
options: only data added to new databases that are added to the eventhouse
only the existing data in the eventhouse
both new data and existing data in the eventhouse
only new data added to the eventhouse

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: only new data added to the eventhouse

Detailed analysis for the Correct Option

Option E: only new data added to the eventhouse Why it is correct: In the Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Intelligence architecture, when you enable the OneLake availability feature at the eventhouse or KQL database level, the native and default behavior of the engine is to strictly synchronize the data that is ingested from the exact moment of activation. Unless the additional "Apply to existing tables" option is explicitly and manually selected during configuration, the system will not perform any historical backfill. Since the question simply states that you "enable OneLake availability" without mentioning additional settings, the default behavior is assumed: only new data ingested after activation will be reflected in OneLake.

  • Official documentation: Enable OneLake availability for KQL databases and eventhouses - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option D: both new data and existing data in the eventhouse Why it is incorrect: This statement would only be true if the administrator had explicitly checked the optional "Apply to existing tables" box when enabling the feature, which would trigger a historical backfill process. Since the scenario does not specify that the default setting was changed, assuming that historical data is automatically copied is a conceptual error frequently tested in the exam.

  • Official documentation: Backfill behavior in OneLake availability - Microsoft Learn

Option B: only the existing data in the eventhouse Why it is incorrect: The OneLake synchronization mechanism is fundamentally a forward-looking, real-time streaming process. There is no setting in Fabric that lets you copy only the static historical data to OneLake while blocking the synchronization of incoming new data.

  • Official documentation: OneLake integration with Real-Time Intelligence - Microsoft Learn

Option A: only data added to new databases that are added to the eventhouse Why it is incorrect: When availability is enabled at the eventhouse level, the replication policy is applied downward. This means that new data ingested into the databases and tables that already existed within the eventhouse will also immediately begin to sync to OneLake, not limited only to databases created afterward.

  • Official documentation: Enabling OneLake at the eventhouse level versus the database level - Microsoft Learn

Option C: no data Why it is incorrect: Enabling OneLake availability has the direct and functional purpose of writing data in Delta Parquet format to OneLake. Stating that no data will be copied completely invalidates the purpose of the feature enabled in the scenario.

  • Official documentation: OneLake and KQL overview - Microsoft Learn

q021.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1.

You plan to integrate Workspace1 with Azure DevOps.

You will use a Fabric deployment pipeline named deployPipeline1 to deploy items from Workspace1 to higher environment workspaces as part of a medallion architecture. You will run deployPipeline1 by using an API call from an Azure DevOps pipeline.

You need to configure API authentication between Azure DevOps and Fabric.

Which type of authentication should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: service principal

Detailed analysis for the Correct Option

Why "service principal" is correct: In continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) scenarios where an external system, such as an Azure DevOps pipeline, needs to interact with the Microsoft Fabric REST APIs in an automated, unattended way (in this case, to run deployPipeline1), the required and recommended identity is a service principal registered in Microsoft Entra ID. This application identity allows secure token-based (OAuth 2.0) authentication at the service-to-service (S2S) level, without requiring user interaction or being interrupted by interactive access policies such as multifactor authentication (MFA).

  • Official documentation: Automate Fabric deployment pipelines (Using service principals) - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Why the other options are incorrect:

B Microsoft Entra username and password: Using interactive user account credentials (username and password) is not a supported or recommended practice for CI/CD automation. These execution flows would systematically fail the moment Microsoft Entra ID required an interactive security challenge to be resolved (such as an MFA sign-in or conditional access policies).

  • Official documentation: Application authentication flows and supported scenarios (Delegated vs. Application) - Microsoft Entra

C managed private endpoint: This is a network architecture concept exclusively, not identity management. A managed private endpoint is used to secure and isolate outbound network traffic from Fabric to an external data source (such as a SQL Server), ensuring that the traffic does not travel over the public internet. It does not provide any kind of API authentication for Azure DevOps.

  • Official documentation: Managed private endpoints in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Fabric

D workspace identity: The workspace identity works in the opposite direction to what this scenario requires. It is used so that the Fabric workspace itself has a managed identity with which to authenticate and securely access external resources (such as Azure Key Vault or Azure Data Lake Storage). It does not allow an external resource (such as Azure DevOps) to sign in or call the Fabric APIs.

  • Official documentation: Workspace identity in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Fabric

q022.stem:
You have a Google Cloud Storage (GCS) container named storage1 that contains the files shown in the following table.

You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that has the cache for shortcuts enabled. Workspace1 contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1.

Lakehouse1 has the shortcuts shown in the following table.

You need to read data from all the shortcuts.

Which shortcuts will retrieve data from the cache?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Stores and Products only

Detailed analysis for the Correct Option

Why "Stores and Products only" is correct: OneLake shortcut caching for cloud sources, such as Google Cloud Storage (GCS), is governed by size and retention rules to optimize performance and minimize network egress costs. To determine which files are retrieved from the current cache, two conditions apply:

  1. File size limit: Individual files larger than 1 GB are not cached. In the scenario, all three files (ProductFile.parquet at 8 MB, StoreFile.json at 500 MB and TripsFile.csv at 99 MB) are smaller than 1 GB, so they are valid candidates.

  2. Default retention period: By default, when the shortcut caching feature is enabled in a workspace, the default retention period is 1 day (24 hours). If a file is not requested within that time interval, it is evicted from the cache.

    • The Stores shortcut was last used 4 hours ago (it is within 24 hours), so it will be read from the cache.

    • The Products shortcut was used 12 hours ago (it is within 24 hours), so it will be read from the cache.

    • The Trips shortcut was accessed 48 hours ago. Having exceeded the default 24-hour inactivity threshold, it has been evicted and its next read will fetch the data directly from GCS.

  • Official documentation: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts (Caching) - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: Stores only / Option B: Products only Why they are incorrect: Both options are incomplete. Each omits one of the two files ("Products" in the case of A, and "Stores" in the case of B) that strictly meet both technical requirements (being smaller than 1 GB and having been accessed within the 24-hour inactivity limit) to be present in and read from the Fabric cache.

  • Official documentation: Shortcut caching configuration and limitations - Microsoft Learn

Option D: Products, Stores, and Trips Why it is incorrect: This option wrongly includes the Trips file. Although the Products and Stores files are cached, the Trips file was last accessed 48 hours ago. Since it exceeded the default 24-hour inactive retention limit, the Fabric engine has already purged it from local storage, which forces the cluster to make a new direct read request (with egress cost) to Google Cloud Storage.

  • Official documentation: Managing the retention period in the OneLake cache - Microsoft Learn

Option E: Trips only / Option F: Products and Trips only Why they are incorrect: Both options fail critically by including the Trips file (TripsFile). The Fabric cache automation rules remove any file that exceeds the retention period without reads (24 hours by default). It is therefore impossible for a query to retrieve from the cache the data of a file that has gone unused for 48 hours; it will always trigger a read from the remote source.

  • Official documentation: Cache retention and removal rules in workspaces - Microsoft Learn
