q082.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1. Workspace1 contains the following items:

• A Dataflow Gen2 dataflow that copies data from an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server database to Lakehouse1

• A notebook that transforms files and loads the data to Lakehouse1 • A data pipeline that loads a CSV file to Lakehouse1

You need to develop an orchestration solution in Fabric that will load each item one after the other. The solution must be scheduled to run every 15 minutes.

Which type of item should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: data pipeline

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Data pipeline: Why it is correct: In the Microsoft Fabric architecture, data pipelines are the native, cloud-based central orchestration engine. Their fundamental purpose is to integrate, schedule and coordinate complex workflows made up of heterogeneous items.

It fully meets the two requirements of the scenario:

  1. Sequencing: It lets you add dedicated activities to the canvas (Dataflow activity, Notebook activity, Invoke pipeline activity) and join them sequentially by using "On success" links, ensuring that each item loads one after another.

  2. Scheduling: It has a robust built-in scheduler that lets you configure exact recurring runs, such as the 15-minute interval the business requires, visually and centrally.

  • Official documentation: Data orchestration with pipelines in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: notebook: Why it is incorrect: Although an Apache Spark notebook has basic scheduling capabilities and can call other notebooks by using utility libraries (mssparkutils), it is not designed to be the main orchestrator of different Fabric items. A notebook runs code (Python, Scala, R) but lacks the native ability to trigger Dataflow Gen2 dataflows or invoke other data pipelines with the reliability, retry control and visualization of an enterprise workflow.

  • Official documentation: Use Apache Spark notebooks in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option B: warehouse: Why it is incorrect: A data warehouse is the relational storage system of Microsoft Fabric designed to support multidimensional data models and run massive analytical queries by using the Transact-SQL language. It is not an orchestration tool, it has no canvas to control workflows, and it has no native features to invoke notebooks or dataflows on a time schedule.

  • Official documentation: What is data warehousing in Microsoft Fabric? - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Dataflow Gen2 dataflow: Why it is incorrect: A Dataflow Gen2 dataflow is a data transformation (ETL) tool powered by the visual Power Query engine. Its purpose is to connect to multiple sources, clean and transform the data, and land it in a destination (such as a lakehouse). Although a dataflow can be scheduled, it does not have the ability to call, trigger or orchestrate Spark notebooks or other dataflows or pipelines. It is a component that is orchestrated, not the one that orchestrates.

  • Official documentation: What is a Dataflow Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric? - Microsoft Learn

q083.stem:
You are building a Fabric notebook named MasterNotebook1 in a workspace.

MasterNotebook1 contains the following code.

You need to ensure that the notebooks are executed in the following sequence:

1. Notebook_03

2. Notebook_01

3. Notebook_02

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
options: Move the declaration of Notebook_02 to the bottom of the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) definition.
Add dependencies to the execution of Notebook_03.
Split the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) definition into three separate definitions.
Add dependencies to the execution of Notebook_02.
Move the declaration of Notebook_03 to the top of the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) definition.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option D: Add dependencies to the execution of Notebook_02.

  • Option F: Move the declaration of Notebook_03 to the top of the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) definition.

Detailed analysis of the correct options

Option D: Add dependencies to the execution of Notebook_02. Why it is correct: In the sequence the business requires, the Notebook_02 notebook must run strictly last (in third position, after Notebook_03 and Notebook_01). To ensure that it waits in a controlled way for the previous tasks to finish, it is mandatory to add the dependencies property ("dependencies") inside the JSON dictionary definition corresponding to execute_notebook_2, linking it to the name of the preceding activity.

  • Official documentation: Orchestrate multiple notebooks and dependencies in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option F: Move the declaration of Notebook_03 to the top of the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) definition. Why it is correct: The business goal requires Notebook_03 to run first (sequence number 1). In the current DAG code snippet, Notebook_03 is declared at the bottom of the activities array. To keep a logical, structured execution order in the graph flow, moving its entire JSON block to the first position at the top of the array properly establishes the starting point of the sequential workflow.

  • Official documentation: DAG structure and design in mssparkutils - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: Move the declaration of Notebook_02 to the bottom of the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) definition. Why it is incorrect: If you review the image of the current code, the execute_notebook_2 block is already naturally positioned in second place (below notebook_01 and before notebook_03). Physically moving it to the end of the array without explicitly configuring its logical dependencies will not force the desired execution order, since the DAG engine evaluates dependency relationships by name and not merely by their visual position in the list.

  • Official documentation: Activity evaluation order in a Spark DAG - Microsoft Learn

Option B: Add dependencies to the execution of Notebook_03. Why it is incorrect: The requirement states that Notebook_03 must be the first to run (1. Notebook_03). If you add dependencies to it so that it waits for another notebook to run, you will break the starting rule, causing it to block unnecessarily instead of starting independently from the beginning of the flow.

  • Official documentation: Designing entry points in execution graphs - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Split the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) definition into three separate definitions. Why it is incorrect: Splitting the code into three distinct DAG structures would force you to call the mssparkutils.notebook.runMultiple method three times consecutively in separate cells. This is completely unnecessary and counterproductive, since the main purpose of runMultiple is precisely to orchestrate multiple notebooks in a centralized, ordered and efficient way within a single DAG dictionary definition.

  • Official documentation: Orchestration best practices with runMultiple - Microsoft Learn

Option E: Change the concurrency to 3. Why it is incorrect: In the current code specification, the "concurrency" parameter is set to 0 (which indicates that the engine will determine the optimal concurrency or that dependencies will be evaluated strictly by the graph). If you change the concurrency to 3, allowing three tasks to run freely at the same time, you will override the linear sequence the business requires (Notebook_03 -> Notebook_01 -> Notebook_02), making the notebooks compete in parallel without respecting the logical order of dependencies.

  • Official documentation: Concurrency control in Spark multiple runs - Microsoft Learn

q084.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a data pipeline named Pipeline1 as shown in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)

What will occur the next time Pipeline1 runs?
options: Copy_kdi will run first, and then Execute procedure1 will run.
Execute procedure1 will run first, and then Copy_kdi will run.
Execute procedure1 will run and Copy_kdi will be skipped.
Copy_kdi will run and Execute procedure1 will be skipped.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Copy_kdi will run and Execute procedure1 will be skipped.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Copy_kdi will run and Execute procedure1 will be skipped: Why it is correct: When analyzing the pipeline canvas provided in the image_be6d27.png file, there are two key visual indicators. First, the activities are not connected by any dependency arrow, which means the engine will try to evaluate them independently. Second, the "Execute procedure1" activity shows a crossed-out circle icon in its upper-left corner, and the history pane at the bottom explicitly confirms that its status (Activity status) is Inactive. In Microsoft Fabric and Azure Data Factory, when you set the state of an activity to Inactive, the pipeline simply ignores it and skips its execution, continuing with the rest of the active activities (such as Copy_kdi).

  • Official documentation: Activity state in pipelines (Active/Inactive) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Copy_kdi will run first, and then Execute procedure1 will run: Why it is incorrect: For a sequential order to exist (one activity first and another after), there must necessarily be a dependency path (a green, blue, red or gray arrow) connecting both boxes on the canvas. Since there is no connection, there is no forced execution order. In addition, the inactive state of the procedure prevents it from running at any point in the flow.

  • Official documentation: Control flow and dependencies between activities - Microsoft Learn

Execute procedure1 will run first, and then Copy_kdi will run: Why it is incorrect: As in the previous option, this statement falsely assumes the existence of a sequential dependency that does not appear in the visual design. Likewise, the stored procedure has its execution disabled by its Inactive state, so it could never run either before or after the data copy.

  • Official documentation: Create and manage dependencies in pipelines - Microsoft Learn

Execute procedure1 will run and Copy_kdi will be skipped: Why it is incorrect: This option describes exactly the reverse of the scenario shown in the actual on-screen configuration. The deactivation icon (the crossed-out circle) falls on the stored procedure, not on the copy activity. Therefore, Copy_kdi is the one that runs and the procedure is the one that is skipped.

  • Official documentation: Temporarily deactivate activities on the canvas - Microsoft Learn

Both activities will run simultaneously: Why it is incorrect: When two activities are placed on the canvas without arrows joining them, the default behavior of the orchestration engine is indeed to launch them in parallel (simultaneously). However, this general rule is overridden here because one of the activities was explicitly marked as Inactive, removing it from the concurrent execution queue.

  • Official documentation: Parallel execution of activities without dependencies - Microsoft Learn

Both activities will be skipped: Why it is incorrect: The Copy_kdi activity has no configured restriction. Its state is not marked as inactive, it does not depend on any other activity that failed, and it is not inside any exclusionary conditional loop. Therefore, the pipeline engine will run it completely normally.

  • Official documentation: Monitor pipeline runs and activity states - Microsoft Learn

q085.stem:
You need to ensure that WorkspaceA can be configured for source control.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
options: From Tenant setting, set Users can synchronize workspace items with their Git repositories to Enabled.
From Tenant setting, set Users can sync workspace items with GitHub repositories to Enabled.
Configure WorkspaceA to use a Premium Per User (PPU) license.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option A: From Tenant setting, set Users can synchronize workspace items with their Git repositories to Enabled.

  • Option D: Assign WorkspaceA to Cap1.

Detailed analysis of the correct options

Option A: From Tenant setting, set Users can synchronize workspace items with their Git repositories to Enabled. Why it is correct: In Microsoft Fabric, version control integration is disabled by default at the global level. For any user to be able to link their workspace to Azure DevOps, a Fabric administrator must go to the admin portal and explicitly turn on the "Users can synchronize workspace items with their Git repositories" switch in the tenant settings. Without this, the Git interface will not be available.

  • Official documentation: Prerequisites and tenant settings for Git integration - Microsoft Learn

Option D: Assign WorkspaceA to Cap1. Why it is correct: The case study states that "WorkspaceA and WorkspaceB currently use the Pro license mode". The Git integration feature is an advanced capability that is not supported in the standard Pro license mode. It strictly requires the workspace to reside on a Premium or Fabric capacity. Since Contoso already has an F64 Fabric capacity named Cap1, the correct architectural action is to reassign WorkspaceA to Cap1, which will automatically unlock the Git functionality.

  • Official documentation: Fabric capacity requirements for Git integration - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option B: From Tenant setting, set Users can sync workspace items with GitHub repositories to Enabled. Why it is incorrect: This admin portal setting is exclusively for enabling the connection with GitHub. The scenario literally states: "Contoso plans to use Azure Repos for version control" and mentions that they already have an "Azure DevOps organization". Therefore, enabling the GitHub switch is entirely irrelevant for this case and will not allow the connection to their Azure DevOps environment.

  • Official documentation: Tenant settings for specific integrations (Azure DevOps vs. GitHub) - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Configure WorkspaceA to use a Premium Per User (PPU) license. Why it is incorrect: Although it is true that a workspace with a PPU license technically enables Git integration, this is the wrong decision for the proposed design. Contoso has already purchased a massive enterprise capacity (F64 named Cap1) that amply covers these requirements. Buying and assigning individual PPU licenses to try to enable this feature would be a redundant cost and would ignore the resources (Cap1) that the case study explicitly provides you to solve the problem.

  • Official documentation: Microsoft Fabric licenses and workspace modes - Microsoft Learn

q086.stem:
HOTSPOT

-

You have a Fabric workspace that contains a warehouse named Warehouse1.

Warehouse1 contains a table named Customer. Customer contains the following data.

You have an internal Microsoft Entra user named User1 that has an email address of [email protected].

You need to provide User1 with access to the Customer table. The solution must prevent User1 from accessing the CreditCard column.

How should you complete the statement? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Dropdown 1: SELECT

  • Dropdown 2: [user1@contoso.com]

Detailed analysis for the correct sequence

Dropdown 1: SELECT Why it is correct: In Transact-SQL (T-SQL), the basic permission that lets a user read or query the data in a table is SELECT. To meet the requirement of preventing access to the credit card column, the syntax shown in the image uses a technique called column-level security. By granting the SELECT permission and explicitly listing in parentheses only the allowed columns (CustomerID, FirstName, LastName, Phone), the SQL engine automatically blocks reading any other column that is not listed, such as CreditCard.

  • Official documentation: GRANT object permissions (Transact-SQL) - Microsoft Learn

Dropdown 2: [user1@contoso.com] Why it is correct: In Microsoft Fabric and Azure SQL, when you grant permissions directly to a Microsoft Entra identity (formerly Azure AD), you must use its user principal name (UPN), which is usually its email address. Because email addresses contain special characters such as the at sign (@) and periods (.), strict SQL syntax requires the full identifier to be enclosed in square brackets []. Therefore, the syntactically correct and functional way to target this Entra ID user is [user1@contoso.com].

  • Official documentation: Security principals (Database Engine) and Microsoft Entra ID - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Incorrect options for Dropdown 1:

ALTER: Why it is incorrect: The ALTER permission lets a user modify the structure of the table (for example, add or drop columns, change data types). It does not grant the ability to query the records (read data) of the table, which is the goal of giving the user access. In addition, column-level syntax is not supported with the ALTER permission in this context.

  • Official documentation: GRANT object permissions (ALTER) - Microsoft Learn

EXECUTE: Why it is incorrect: The EXECUTE permission is designed exclusively to allow the execution of code modules such as stored procedures or user-defined functions (UDFs). It is not a valid command to apply on tables or views, so the SQL engine will return an immediate syntax error.

  • Official documentation: GRANT object permissions (EXECUTE) - Microsoft Learn

READ: Why it is incorrect: READ is not a valid permission keyword in Transact-SQL for interacting with tables at the object level. The standard SQL command for granting data read rights is SELECT. Trying to use READ will cause a compilation failure.

  • Official documentation: Transact-SQL syntax conventions - Microsoft Learn

VIEW: Why it is incorrect: T-SQL has the VIEW DEFINITION permission, which lets a user see the metadata (structure and schema) of an object, but does not let them query the row data. The word VIEW by itself is not a permission that can be applied in a GRANT statement to read the contents of a table.

  • Official documentation: GRANT database permissions (VIEW DEFINITION) - Microsoft Learn

Incorrect options for Dropdown 2:

User1: Why it is incorrect: If you use the name User1 without brackets and without the Entra ID domain, the SQL engine will assume you are referencing a local database user (SQL authentication) with that exact name. Since the scenario specifies that it is a Microsoft Entra user identified by their email address, the principal mapping will fail and the permission will not be applied to the right user.

  • Official documentation: CREATE USER (Transact-SQL) - Microsoft Learn

[User1]: Why it is incorrect: Although adding brackets solves potential syntax problems (useful if the name had spaces), it still has the same error as the previous option: it does not include the email domain (@contoso.com). Microsoft Fabric requires the full Entra ID UPN for direct authentication, so targeting [User1] will generate a principal-not-found error.

  • Official documentation: Database identifiers (brackets and quotes) - Microsoft Learn

q087.stem:
You need to create a workflow for the new book cover images.

Which two components should you include in the workflow? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
options: a notebook that uses Apache Spark Structured Streaming

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option C: A data pipeline

  • Option D: A blob storage action

Detailed analysis for the correct options

Option D: A blob storage action

  • Why it is correct: The case study imposes a very strict timing requirement: the new book cover image must be processed "as soon as possible" once it arrives in the folder. To achieve this without introducing latency (waiting), the technical solution must be event-based. In Microsoft Fabric, pipelines can be connected to storage event triggers. This component watches the underlying OneLake storage and, the exact moment it detects the creation of a new file, it starts the workflow automatically and reactively, while also complying with the guideline of using only native Fabric items.

  • Official documentation: Create storage event triggers in Fabric pipelines - Microsoft Learn

Option C: A data pipeline

  • Why it is correct: The data pipeline is the central orchestration engine of Microsoft Fabric. To meet the goal of creating a "workflow" that processes the new image, you need a container that orchestrates and hosts the activities to run. The data pipeline is natively designed to link directly with the storage event trigger (the blob action) and immediately start the required compute steps in response to that arrival event.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to data pipelines in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option: A reflex item

  • Why it is incorrect: The "reflex item" was the preliminary name (in Preview) of what is now known as Data Activator in Microsoft Fabric. This component is designed to evaluate business conditions on data (for example, detecting whether sales fall below a threshold in a Power BI report) and trigger alerts. It is not designed to monitor infrastructure events at the file system level (such as the physical creation of a binary image in a storage folder). To capture file storage events, the designated tool is the pipeline trigger.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to Data Activator in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option: A time-based schedule

  • Why it is incorrect: A scheduled trigger runs workflows at predefined time intervals (for example, every 15 minutes or every hour). If an image is uploaded to the folder just after a run has finished, the file has to wait idle until the next cycle. This directly violates the business requirement to process the images "as soon as possible" (zero latency).

  • Official documentation: Run pipelines on a schedule - Microsoft Learn

Option: A notebook that uses Apache Spark Structured Streaming

  • Why it is incorrect: Although Spark Structured Streaming can monitor directories for new files continuously (through structured streams), it would require keeping an Apache Spark compute cluster on and consuming resources non-stop (24/7) just to watch for the sporadic arrival of images. This would generate massive and unnecessary consumption of capacity units (CUs), which directly violates the governance and cost-control requirements of the data platform.

  • Official documentation: Apache Spark Structured Streaming in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option: A streaming dataflow

  • Why it is incorrect: Streaming dataflows are oriented to and optimized for ingesting continuous streams of structured or semi-structured data (such as IoT telemetry sensor signals or real-time JSON records) and connecting them to semantic models. They do not have the architecture or the capability to orchestrate workflows based on the arrival of unstructured binary files, such as JPEG or PNG book cover images.

  • Official documentation: Eventstreams overview in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option C: A notebook that uses Apache Spark Structured Streaming Why it is incorrect: Although Spark Structured Streaming can process data streams, setting up a notebook to listen to a REST API non-stop requires keeping a Spark cluster on 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. This would generate extremely high capacity unit (CU) consumption, which directly violates the business requirement to "control the costs of the data platform". You have a Fabric warehouse named DW1 that contains four staging tables named ProductCategory, ProductSubcategory, Product, and SalesOrder.

ProductCategory, ProductSubcategory, and Product are used often in analytical queries.

You need to implement a star schema for DW1. The solution must minimize development effort.

Which design approach should you use? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Dropdown 1: Denormalized into a single product dimension table

  • Dropdown 2: The unique system generated identifier

Detailed analysis for the correct sequence

Dropdown 1: Denormalized into a single product dimension table Why it is correct: The main requirement of the scenario is to implement a star schema. In a pure star schema, the model consists of a central fact table (sales) surrounded by denormalized dimension tables. Keeping the category, subcategory and product in three separate tables creates a snowflake schema. To meet the star schema goal, you must consolidate (denormalize) those three hierarchical levels into a single product dimension table.

  • Official documentation: Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI - Microsoft Learn

Dropdown 2: The unique system generated identifier Why it is correct: In dimensional modeling, the standard best practice is for relationships between fact tables and dimension tables to be established by using surrogate keys. A surrogate key is exactly a "unique system generated identifier" (usually an auto-incrementing integer). This ensures optimal join performance and isolates the analytical model from possible changes to the natural keys of the source system.

  • Official documentation: Design dimension tables (using surrogate keys) - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Incorrect options for Dropdown 1:

Added to the model as individual tables: Why it is incorrect: If you add Product, Subcategory and Category as three individual tables related in a chain, you are building a snowflake schema. Although this is a valid model in traditional relational databases, it directly fails the requirement of the problem, which demands implementing a star schema. It also requires more development effort by forcing the engine to process multiple joins for a simple query by category.

  • Official documentation: Snowflake schema vs. star schema - Microsoft Learn

Denormalized by being added to the SalesOrder table: Why it is incorrect: This option proposes flattening all the product and category descriptions directly into the sales fact table (SalesOrder). This creates a single flat table model. Doing this completely destroys the concept of a star schema, generates massive data redundancy (the category name would be repeated for every individual sale) and severely degrades the performance of the analytical model.

  • Official documentation: Drawbacks of fully denormalized tables - Microsoft Learn

Incorrect options for Dropdown 2:

The product name and the date: Why it is incorrect: Using the product name and a date as the join key means using a text-based composite key. In columnar analytical engines such as VertiPaq or in Fabric data warehouse storage, joining tables on text strings consumes a lot of memory and CPU, ruining performance. In addition, a product name can change in the source system, which would break the historical relationship with past sales.

  • Official documentation: Performance impact of using text columns in relationships - Microsoft Learn

The product category name: Why it is incorrect: The product category name does not have the granularity needed to uniquely identify a specific product. A category groups hundreds of different products. If you try to join the sales table to the product dimension by using the category name, you will create a many-to-many relationship that multiplies the records (Cartesian product) and returns completely wrong financial calculations.

  • Official documentation: Granularity in dimensional modeling - Microsoft Learn

Your company has three newly created data engineering teams named Team1, Team2, and Team3 that plan to use Fabric. The teams have the following personas:

• Team1 consists of members who currently use Microsoft Power BI. The team wants to transform data by using by a low-code approach.

• Team2 consists of members that have a background in Python programming.

The team wants to use PySpark code to transform data.

• Team3 consists of members who currently use Azure Data Factory. The team wants to move data between source and sink environments by using the least amount of effort.

You need to recommend tools for the teams based on their current personas.

What should you recommend for each team? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Dropdown 1 (Team1): Dataflow Gen2 dataflow

  • Dropdown 2 (Team2): Notebooks

  • Dropdown 3 (Team3): Data pipelines

Detailed analysis for the correct sequence

Dropdown 1 (Team1): Dataflow Gen2 dataflow Why it is correct: Team 1 has prior experience with Power BI and wants a low-code solution. In the Microsoft Fabric ecosystem, Dataflow Gen2 is built directly on the Power Query Online engine, which is exactly the same visual data transformation interface these users already know from Power BI. It lets you clean and transform data by dragging and dropping, without having to write complex code.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to Dataflows Gen2 - Microsoft Learn

Dropdown 2 (Team2): Notebooks Why it is correct: Team 2 is made up of Python developers who want to write PySpark code explicitly. Apache Spark notebooks in Fabric are the native integrated development environment (IDE) designed for data scientists and data engineers. They natively support PySpark code cells, allowing interactive execution, exploratory analysis and fully code-based data transformation.

  • Official documentation: How to use notebooks in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Dropdown 3 (Team3): Data pipelines Why it is correct: Team 3 comes from Azure Data Factory (ADF) and its goal is to move data from a source to a sink with minimal effort. Data pipelines in Fabric are the direct evolution of Azure Data Factory. They share the same interface, logic and main activities, such as the Copy data activity, which lets you perform bulk ingestion from source to destination through a visual wizard in just a few clicks, minimizing the effort entirely.

  • Official documentation: Compare Azure Data Factory and Data Factory in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Incorrect options for Dropdown 1 (Team1):

Data pipelines: Why it is incorrect: Although data pipelines have a graphical interface, their main purpose is workflow orchestration and bulk data copying, not deep row-by-row or column-by-column data transformation. They do not use Power Query, so the Power BI team would lose its familiar low-code environment for data cleaning.

  • Official documentation: Data pipeline concepts - Microsoft Learn

Notebooks: Why it is incorrect: Notebooks necessarily require advanced programming knowledge (Python, Scala, R or SQL). This directly violates Team 1's requirement, which calls for a low-code approach. Forcing Power BI analysts to write code in Spark would drastically increase the learning curve.

  • Official documentation: Develop and run notebooks in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Incorrect options for Dropdown 2 (Team2):

Data pipelines: Why it is incorrect: Data pipelines are visual orchestration tools. They do not provide a console or an editor for writing PySpark scripts. A Python engineer cannot develop the data transformation logic inside the pipeline canvas; they can only use the pipeline to invoke a notebook that has already been written beforehand.

  • Official documentation: Activities supported in data pipelines - Microsoft Learn

Dataflow Gen2 dataflow: Why it is incorrect: Dataflow Gen2 is a tool based on a graphical interface (Power Query) that generates M language code underneath. It does not support writing, running or integrating Python or PySpark scripts. Assigning this tool to Team 2 would completely waste their Python programming skills.

  • Official documentation: Differences between Dataflow Gen2 and Spark notebooks - Microsoft Learn

Incorrect options for Dropdown 3 (Team3):

Notebooks: Why it is incorrect: To move data from source to destination by using a notebook, the team would have to write the code to establish the connections, mount the paths, read the data into a DataFrame and then write that DataFrame to the destination. This requires significant coding effort and does not take advantage of the team's prior experience with the Azure Data Factory visual interface.

  • Official documentation: Read and write data by using Spark notebooks - Microsoft Learn

Dataflow Gen2 dataflow: Why it is incorrect: Although Dataflow Gen2 can read from a source and write to a destination, it is designed mainly to apply complex step-by-step transformation logic (ETL). If the goal is simply to move the data as is (source to sink) with the "least effort possible", the Copy data activity in data pipelines is immensely faster, is optimized for bulk loads and is the natural environment for Azure Data Factory users.

  • Official documentation: Choose between Dataflows Gen2 and data pipelines - Microsoft Learn

You plan to process the following three datasets by using Fabric:

Dataset1: This dataset will be added to Fabric and will have a unique primary key between the source and the destination. The unique primary key will be an integer and will start from 1 and have an increment of 1.

Dataset2: This dataset contains semi-structured data that uses bulk data transfer. The dataset must be handled in one process between the source and the destination. The data transformation process will include the use of custom visuals to understand and work with the dataset in development mode.

Dataset3: This dataset is in a lakehouse. The data will be bulk loaded. The data transformation process will include row-based windowing functions during the loading process.

You need to identify which type of item to use for the datasets. The solution must minimize development effort and use built-in functionality, when possible.

What should you identify for each dataset? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Dropdown 1 (Dataset1): Dataflow Gen2 dataflow

  • Dropdown 2 (Dataset2): A notebook

  • Dropdown 3 (Dataset3): A T-SQL statement

Detailed analysis for the correct options

Dropdown 1 (Dataset1): Dataflow Gen2 dataflow Why it is correct: The requirement specifies creating a unique primary key that starts at 1 and increments by 1, with the strict goal of minimizing development effort and using built-in functionality. In Microsoft Fabric, Dataflow Gen2 includes a native feature in its visual interface called Add index column. This tool generates exactly this number sequence with a single click, without having to write or maintain a single line of code.

  • Official documentation: Add an index column in Power Query - Microsoft Learn

Dropdown 2 (Dataset2): A notebook Why it is correct: The scenario requires processing semi-structured data and using custom images in the development mode. In the Microsoft Fabric architecture, Apache Spark compute environments (which run through notebooks) are the only data processing component that lets you attach and configure custom container (Docker) images. This lets developers install operating system or Python specific libraries to handle complex data structures.

  • Official documentation: Create and use custom environments in Fabric (custom images) - Microsoft Learn

Dropdown 3 (Dataset3): A T-SQL statement Why it is correct: The requirement is to bulk load data from a lakehouse while applying row-based window functions during the load. Transact-SQL (T-SQL) has native, robust and highly optimized support for window functions through the OVER clause (for example, functions such as ROW_NUMBER or RANK). In Fabric, you can use T-SQL statements through cross-database queries to read from the lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint and transform the data efficiently during the insert.

  • Official documentation: Window functions in T-SQL (OVER clause) - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Incorrect options for Dropdown 1 (Dataset1):

A notebook: Why it is incorrect: Although it is technically possible to generate an incremental sequence in a PySpark notebook (by using the monotonically_increasing_id function combined with window functions), this requires writing, testing and debugging complex code. This directly violates the business requirement to minimize development effort when a native visual tool exists that does it automatically.

  • Official documentation: ID generation limitations in PySpark - Microsoft Learn

A T-SQL statement: Why it is incorrect: Creating an auto-incrementing field with T-SQL requires defining an IDENTITY property when creating the table or managing a SEQUENCE object. As with the notebook, it requires writing manual data definition language (DDL) code, which is more effort than using the prebuilt graphical interface of a dataflow.

  • Official documentation: IDENTITY property (Transact-SQL) - Microsoft Learn

Incorrect options for Dropdown 2 (Dataset2):

Dataflow Gen2 dataflow: Why it is incorrect: Dataflow Gen2 is a managed software service based on the Power Query engine. It does not let developers modify its underlying infrastructure, nor does it support loading Docker container images to customize the data processing environment.

  • Official documentation: Dataflow Gen2 architecture - Microsoft Learn

A T-SQL statement: Why it is incorrect: The SQL data warehousing engine in Microsoft Fabric is a fully managed cloud service (SaaS). It has no functionality that lets users deploy or mount custom containers or images to alter the compute environment of queries.

  • Official documentation: T-SQL surface area in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Incorrect options for Dropdown 3 (Dataset3):

Dataflow Gen2 dataflow: Why it is incorrect: The Power Query engine (Dataflow Gen2) lacks a direct and efficient visual interface for applying analytic window functions based on row partitions. Trying to replicate this logic would require writing very advanced manual scripts in M language, which maximizes development effort and drastically penalizes performance in bulk loads.

  • Official documentation: Modeling and transformation concepts in Power Query - Microsoft Learn

A KQL queryset: Why it is incorrect: Kusto Query Language (KQL) is designed and optimized mainly for exploring and analyzing real-time streaming telemetry (streaming logs). It is not the standard tool, nor the one recommended in Fabric, for bulk extract and load (ETL) processes that require intensive use of traditional relational window functions.

  • Official documentation: KQL database overview in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

You have a Fabric workspace that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1.

Lakehouse1 contains a table named Status_Target that has the following columns:

• Key

• Status

• LastModified

The data source contains a table named Status_Source that has the same columns as Status_Target. Status_Source is used to populate Status_Target.

In a notebook name Notebook1, you load Status_Source to a DataFrame named sourceDF and Status_Target to a DataFrame named targetDF.

You need to implement an incremental loading pattern by using Notebook1. The solution must meet the following requirements:

• For all the matching records that have the same value of key, update the value of LastModified in Status_Target to the value of LastModified in Status_Source. • Insert all the records that exist in Status_Source that do NOT exist in Status_Target.

• Set the value of Status in Status_Target to inactive for all the records that were last modified more than seven days ago and that do NOT exist in Status_Source.

How should you complete the statement? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Dropdown 1: .whenMatchedUpdate(

  • Dropdown 2: .whenNotMatchedInsert(

  • Dropdown 3: .whenNotMatchedBySourceUpdate(

Detailed analysis for the correct sequence

Dropdown 1: .whenMatchedUpdate( Why it is correct: The first requirement states that "for all matching records that have the same key value, update the value". In the structured Delta Lake API for PySpark, the clause designed specifically to modify records in the target table when the join condition (sourceDF.Key = targetDF.Key) is true is whenMatchedUpdate. This function takes the dictionary of values provided in the set variable and overwrites the corresponding column in the target.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake merge operations (WHEN MATCHED clause) - Microsoft Learn

Dropdown 2: .whenNotMatchedInsert( Why it is correct: The second requirement says "Insert all records that exist in Status_Source that do NOT exist in Status_Target". The Delta API handles inserts of new records coming from the source dataset by using the whenNotMatchedInsert clause. This function fires exclusively when a source row does not find its corresponding key in the target, inserting the values defined in the values dictionary.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake merge operations (WHEN NOT MATCHED clause) - Microsoft Learn

Dropdown 3: .whenNotMatchedBySourceUpdate( Why it is correct: The third requirement calls for changing the status to inactive for the records "that do NOT exist in Status_Source". Starting with modern versions of Delta Lake, a family of "BySource" functions was introduced to handle logical deletes or updates on orphaned records. The whenNotMatchedBySourceUpdate clause evaluates the records that currently live in the target table but have disappeared from the input dataset (the source), allowing you to natively apply the date condition and the status update to "inactive".

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake merge operations (WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE clause) - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Since the three dropdowns share the same list of Delta Lake API options, the following explains why the remaining functions are incorrect or logically impossible for each code block:

.whenMatchedInsert( Why it is incorrect: This function is a logical contradiction in upsert (merge) operations. You cannot run an insert command on a row that has already met the match condition (matched) in the target table, because the primary key already exists and a duplication or a constraint error would result. It is therefore invalid in any of the three dropdowns.

  • Official documentation: MERGE INTO statement semantics in Delta Lake - Microsoft Learn

.whenNotMatchedBySourceInsert( Why it is incorrect: Another logical contradiction in the API. The "BySource" family of functions evaluates records that exist in the target but are missing from the source. It is physically impossible to insert a record from the source into the target if the premise of the function is precisely that the record does not exist in the source. The Spark engine will return a compilation error.

  • Official documentation: Limitations of BySource clauses in Delta Lake - Microsoft Learn

.whenNotMatchedUpdate( Why it is incorrect: The standard "NotMatched" clause evaluates the new records coming from the source that are not yet in the target table. You cannot perform an update operation on a row that does not yet exist in the target storage. The only valid action for a standard "NotMatched" record is insertion.

  • Official documentation: Validation rules for NotMatched clauses - Microsoft Learn

.whenMatchedUpdate( (If used in blocks 2 or 3) Why it is incorrect: If it is selected in block 2 (new inserts) or block 3 (orphaned records from the source), the code will fail to meet the business requirements. This function can only interact with records where the key is identical in both tables, completely ignoring new records or logically deleted ones.

  • Official documentation: WHEN MATCHED clause behavior - Microsoft Learn

.whenNotMatchedInsert( (If used in blocks 1 or 3) Why it is incorrect: Using this function in the first block would try to apply insert logic to records that already exist. If it is used in the third block, it would ignore the need to update the old records in the target, limiting itself to only adding the new records from the source.

  • Official documentation: WHEN NOT MATCHED clause behavior - Microsoft Learn

You are building a data loading pattern by using a Fabric data pipeline. The source is an Azure SQL database that contains 25 tables. The destination is a lakehouse.

In a warehouse, you create a control table named Control.Object as shown in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)

You need to build a data pipeline that will support the dynamic ingestion of the tables listed in the control table by using a single execution.

Which three actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Box 1: Add a Lookup activity to query Control.Object and generate a list of the schemas and tables to copy.

  • Box 2: Add a ForEach activity to iterate over the list of tables and copy the source data to the lakehouse Delta tables.

  • Box 3: Add a Copy data activity as an inner activity to the iterator activity.

Detailed analysis for the correct sequence

Box 1: Add a Lookup activity to query Control.Object and generate a list of the schemas and tables to copy. Why it is correct: The first logical step in a dynamic load pattern (metadata-driven) is to read the configuration stored in the database. The Lookup activity is designed exactly to run a SQL query against the Control.Object table and return the results (the schemas and names of the 25 tables) in a JSON array format that the rest of the pipeline can understand and process.

  • Official documentation: Control table-based bulk copy pattern (Step 1: Lookup) - Microsoft Learn

Box 2: Add a ForEach activity to iterate over the list of tables and copy the source data to the lakehouse Delta tables. Why it is correct: Once the Lookup activity returns the list of tables, you need a mechanism that processes each of them. The ForEach activity acts as an iterator loop that receives the JSON array produced in the previous step and walks through it item by item (table by table), running a set of actions for each record found.

  • Official documentation: ForEach activity in data pipelines - Microsoft Learn

Box 3: Add a Copy data activity as an inner activity to the iterator activity. Why it is correct: The final step is to perform the physical movement of the data. This action must be configured inside the ForEach loop (as an inner activity). The Copy data activity will dynamically take the schema and table parameters that the ForEach loop injects on each iteration, extracting the data from Azure SQL and landing it in the lakehouse.

  • Official documentation: Configure inner activities within a ForEach - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Add a Get metadata activity to query Control.Object and generate a list of schemas and tables to copy. Why it is incorrect: The Get metadata activity is used to inspect the properties of files or directories in a storage system (for example, to find out whether a file exists, its size, or to list the files in a folder). It is not designed for, nor does it have the capability to, run SQL queries (SELECT) against a relational table (Control.Object) to read its contents as rows. That is exclusively the job of the Lookup activity.

  • Official documentation: Get metadata activity use cases - Microsoft Learn

Add an Until activity to iterate over the list of tables and copy the source data to the lakehouse Delta tables. Why it is incorrect: The Until activity is a conditional loop (equivalent to a "do-while" in programming) that runs repeatedly until a specific condition evaluates to true (for example, "run until a file appears"). It is not a collection iterator. It cannot ingest a list (array) of tables and walk through it row by row, so it is the wrong tool for iterating over the results of a control table.

  • Official documentation: Differences between ForEach and Until loops - Microsoft Learn

q094.stem:
You are implementing a medallion architecture in a Fabric lakehouse.

You plan to create a dimension table that will contain the following columns:

• ID

• CustomerCode

• CustomerName

• CustomerAddress

• CustomerLocation

• ValidFrom

• ValidTo

You need to ensure that the table supports the analysis of historical sales data by customer location at the time of each sale.

Which type of slowly changing dimension (SCD) should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Type 2

Detailed analysis for the correct option

Option A: Type 2 Why it is correct: The main requirement calls for the ability to analyze historical data by relating sales to the location the customer had exactly "at the time of each sale". The Type 2 slowly changing dimension (SCD) is the only dimensional design pattern that preserves the full, continuous history of a record. It does so by inserting a new row (with a new surrogate key ID) every time the customer changes location, instead of overwriting the old record. The presence of the ValidFrom and ValidTo columns in the provided schema is the unmistakable technical signature of a Type 2 SCD model, since these columns mark the exact period of time during which each version of the customer record was active.

  • Official documentation: Slowly changing dimensions (Type 2 SCD) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option B: Type 0 Why it is incorrect: The Type 0 SCD model (retain original) completely ignores any future changes to attributes. Once the customer is inserted for the first time, their location is never updated and no new rows are created. This model neither requires nor uses date control columns such as ValidFrom or ValidTo, and it is useless for tracking the history of a customer's location changes over time.

  • Official documentation: Dimension design patterns (Type 0 SCD) - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Type 1 Why it is incorrect: The Type 1 SCD model (overwrite) updates the existing record directly when a change occurs, destroying and replacing the previous value. If a customer moves, their new location overwrites the old one. As a result, all historical sales for that customer will appear associated with their current location, which flatly fails the business requirement to see the data as it was "at the time of the sale". It also does not use temporal columns.

  • Official documentation: Handling attribute changes (Type 1 SCD) - Microsoft Learn

Option D: Type 3 Why it is incorrect: The Type 3 SCD model keeps a very limited history by adding extra columns to the same record instead of adding new rows. For example, it would use columns such as CurrentLocation and PreviousLocation. Its structure is not based on validity periods (ValidFrom and ValidTo) and it does not scale if a customer changes location three or more times, so it does not match the schema presented in the question.

  • Official documentation: Comparison of changing dimensions (Type 3 SCD) - Microsoft Learn

q095.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains an eventstream named EventStream1. EventStream1 outputs events to a table named Table1 in a lakehouse. The streaming data is sourced from motorway sensors and represents the speed of cars.

You need to add a transformation to EventStream1 to average the car speeds.

The speeds must be grouped by non-overlapping and contiguous time intervals of one minute. Each event must belong to exactly one window.

Which windowing function should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: tumbling

Detailed analysis for the correct option

Option C: tumbling Why it is correct: In event stream processing in Microsoft Fabric and Azure, a tumbling window function (also known as a fixed-size, non-overlapping window) is defined by two fundamental characteristics that fit the case study perfectly: the windows are contiguous and do not overlap. When you configure a one-minute tumbling window, the analytics engine splits the timeline into rigid, discrete and consecutive blocks (for example, from 10:00:00 to 10:01:00, and the next one from 10:01:00 to 10:02:00). Since the edges of these windows never overlap, it is mathematically guaranteed that each sensor speed reading will belong to one, and absolutely only one, time grouping for calculating its average.

  • Official documentation: Tumbling window functions (fixed-size hops) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: sliding Why it is incorrect: The sliding window evaluates data aggregates by looking at the stream over a time interval that advances continuously, producing results only when the content of the window changes (that is, when a car enters or leaves the time range). Because of this smooth, constant movement along the timeline, the windows overlap massively. The same speed record will be included repeatedly in multiple overlapping windows, which flatly fails the single-membership requirement and the non-overlap rule.

  • Official documentation: Sliding window functions - Microsoft Learn

Option B: hopping Why it is incorrect: Hopping windows model scheduled windows that move forward in time by a defined hop period, but their size (duration) is usually larger than that hop step. For example, you could configure a 5-minute window that advances (hops) every 1 minute. This structural behavior causes the windows to overlap with each other intentionally. As with the previous option, this causes a single event to be processed and assigned to several groupings at the same time, violating the business rules.

  • Official documentation: Hopping window functions - Microsoft Learn

Option D: session Why it is incorrect: Session windows have dynamic behavior and lack a fixed time size. They group events that occur at similar times (bursts of data) and filter out periods of inactivity by closing the window when a predetermined amount of time passes without receiving new data. Since the business requirement explicitly demands splitting time into identical, fixed mathematical intervals of "one minute", using a window of unpredictable, dynamic length based on inactivity times is the wrong strategy.

You have a notebook that contains the following code segment.

  • Statement 2: No

  • Statement 3: No

Detailed analysis of the statements

Statement 1: Line 01 will replace all null and empty values in the CustomerName column with the value Unknown. Answer: Yes Why it is correct: Line 01 uses the PySpark when function to evaluate a compound Boolean condition: (col("CustomerName").isNull() | (col("CustomerName")=="")). If the column is null (isNull) or completely empty (""), the lit("Unknown") function injects the text string "Unknown". If neither of these conditions is met, the .otherwise(col("CustomerName")) clause keeps the original customer name. This is the exact and correct syntax to achieve this replacement behavior in the Spark structured API.

Statement 2: Line 02 will extract the value before the @ character and generate a new column named Username. Answer: No Why it is incorrect: The statement is false because of the behavior of the getItem(1) method. Line 02 uses the split(col("Email"), "@") function, which splits the email address into an array of two elements. In C-based programming arrays (such as those in Spark), the index always starts at zero (0). Therefore:

  • getItem(0) extracts the part before the @ character (e.g. "brian23").

  • getItem(1) extracts the part after the @ character (e.g. "adventure-works.com"). Line 02 in the code extracts the domain, not the username.

Statement 3: Line 03 will extract the year value from the OrderDate column and keep only the first occurrence of each year. Answer: No Why it is incorrect: Line 03 in the code performs the dropDuplicates(["OrderDate"]) action. This tells the Spark engine to find and remove records based exclusively on the full value of the OrderDate column (for example, "2021-01-01"), before any year extraction takes place. If you look at the source table, all the rows have exactly the same order date ("2021-01-01"). Therefore, dropDuplicates will remove all rows from the table except the first, based on the exact January date, not on the year. The year extraction happens in the subsequent .select, but by that point the other rows have already been deleted.

In Eventhouse1, you plan to create a table named DeviceStreamData in a KQL database. The table will contain data based on the following sample.

Box 3: StreamData:dynamic ) Why it is correct: The StreamData column in the sample image stores complex semi-structured data: an array that contains JSON objects (with nested properties such as index, eventId, isActive, latitude). q098.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a warehouse named Warehouse1.

You have an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server database named Database1 that is accessed by using an on-premises data gateway.

You need to copy data from Database1 to Warehouse1.

Which item should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: A data pipeline

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option A: A data pipeline. Why it is correct: In the Microsoft Fabric architecture, data pipelines are the main tool for enterprise-level data movement (ETL/ELT). The Copy data activity inside a pipeline has native, direct support for integrating with the on-premises data gateway. This lets you configure a secure connection to your on-premises SQL Server database, extract the data and write it natively to the Fabric warehouse, all through a graphical interface and without needing complex network configuration in the cloud.

  • Official documentation: Access on-premises data sources in Data Factory pipelines (Gateway) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option B: an Apache Spark job definition Why it is incorrect: Apache Spark job definitions are used to submit batch jobs that run on the Spark compute engine. The architectural problem here is that Spark clusters in Fabric cannot route their traffic through the standard on-premises data gateway. For Spark to access on-premises networks, a different network infrastructure is required, such as a virtual network (VNet) data gateway or private endpoints. Therefore, using the standard gateway with this item does not work.

  • Official documentation: Network and connectivity considerations for Apache Spark in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option C: A streaming dataflow Why it is incorrect: A streaming dataflow is an item designed exclusively to capture, transform and route continuous real-time telemetry or events (for example, from Azure Event Hubs or IoT sensors). It is not a batch extraction tool designed to connect to on-premises relational databases, nor does it integrate with the on-premises data gateway to run SQL queries against a traditional database.

  • Official documentation: Supported sources for streaming dataflows - Microsoft Learn

Option D: A notebook Why it is incorrect: Like job definitions, notebooks run on the Apache Spark engine. This engine lacks native connectivity to bridge JDBC connections to on-premises databases by using the standard on-premises data gateway installed on Windows servers. It would also require writing manual extraction code and dealing with network limitations, whereas the data pipeline is built exactly to solve this architecture pattern with minimal effort.

  • Official documentation: Limitations of accessing on-premises data with Spark notebooks - Microsoft Learn

q099.stem:
You have a Fabric warehouse named DW1 that contains a Type 2 slowly changing dimension (SCD) dimension table named DimCustomer. DimCustomer contains 100 columns and 20 million rows. The columns are of various data types, including int, varchar, date, and varbinary.

You need to identify incoming changes to the table and update the records when there is a change. The solution must minimize resource consumption.

What should you use to identify changes to attributes?
options: a hash function to compare the attributes in the source table.
a direct attributes comparison across the attributes in the DimCustomer table.
a direct attributes comparison for the attributes in the source table.
a hash function to compare the attributes in the DimCustomer table.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: A hash function to compare the attributes in the source table.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option A: a hash function to compare the attributes in the source table. Why it is correct: In modern dimensional modeling for large data warehouses in Microsoft Fabric, handling slowly changing dimension (SCD Type 2) tables that have 100 columns and 20 million rows presents an enormous computational challenge. The recommended architecture practice to minimize resource consumption (CPU and memory) is the Hash Key / Checksum pattern. During the load process (ETL), instead of evaluating each attribute individually, a hash function (such as HASHBYTES in T-SQL) is generated that concatenates the 100 columns of the incoming data in the source table. This single incoming hash value is compared with the matching hash column that is already materialized and statically stored in the target table (DimCustomer). This way, the SQL engine goes from evaluating 100 logical conditions to comparing a single field, which speeds up change detection and drastically minimizes capacity resource consumption.

  • Official documentation: Dimensional modeling and SCD dimension loading guide in a data warehouse - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option D: a hash function to compare the attributes in the DimCustomer table. Why it is incorrect: This is the main trap of the question. If you configure your process to dynamically compute the hash function by reading the attributes of the target table (DimCustomer) while the join query runs, you force the Fabric cluster to compute a cryptographic algorithm over 100 columns for each of the 20 million historical rows on every run. This would consume a colossal amount of compute resources. The target hash must already be precomputed and stored as a persistent physical column; the runtime computation is done only over the small volume of the source table.

  • Official documentation: Dynamic computation anti-patterns and optimization in Synapse and Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option B: a direct attributes comparison across the attributes in the DimCustomer table. Why it is incorrect: A direct attribute comparison would mean writing a SQL statement (JOIN or MERGE) with 100 logical conditions (Target.Col1 <> Source.Col1 OR Target.Col2 <> Source.Col2...). On a massive table of 20 million records in the target, forcing the engine to evaluate dozens of columns of different data types (varchar, dates, varbinary) will generate an extremely heavy table scan and high CPU consumption, violating the main requirement of "minimizing resource consumption".

  • Official documentation: Query performance guidelines in data warehousing - Microsoft Learn

Option C: a direct attributes comparison for the attributes in the source table. Why it is incorrect: For the same reason as option B, performing a direct field-by-field (attribute-by-attribute) check from the source to the target is the least efficient technique possible in data engineering for wide tables (100 columns). The engine would waste memory and processing time evaluating varbinary or varchar columns individually when the hash pattern solves the problem with a single string validation.

  • Official documentation: Data type and performance considerations in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

q100.stem:
You have an Azure SQL database named DB1.

In a Fabric workspace, you deploy an eventstream named EventStreamDB1 to stream record changes from DB1 into a lakehouse.

You discover that events are NOT being propagated to EventStreamDB1.

You need to ensure that the events are propagated to EventStreamDB1.

What should you do?
options: Create a read-only replica of DB1.
Create an Azure Stream Analytics job.
Enable change data capture (CDC) for DB1.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Enable change data capture (CDC) for DB1.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option D: Enable change data capture (CDC) for DB1. Why it is correct: In Microsoft Fabric, the native eventstream connector designed to ingest data from an Azure SQL database works by reading the transaction logs by using Change Data Capture (CDC) technology. If this feature is not explicitly enabled both at the database level and at the level of the specific tables in Azure SQL, the eventstream engine has no way to detect insert, update or delete operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE). When you enable CDC, the database starts recording these changes in system tables, allowing the eventstream to read them and propagate them to the lakehouse continuously.

  • Official documentation: Add an Azure SQL Database source to an eventstream (CDC prerequisites) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: Create a read-only replica of DB1. Why it is incorrect: A read-only replica (read scale-out) is an architecture feature designed to divert heavy read queries (such as reporting) away from the primary transactional database, thereby improving overall performance. However, a replica does not natively generate or transmit a row-level stream of data change events to external services such as a Fabric eventstream.

  • Official documentation: Use read-only replicas to load-balance workloads - Microsoft Learn

Option B: Create an Azure Stream Analytics job. Why it is incorrect: A Fabric eventstream is already the native real-time routing and processing tool of Microsoft Fabric. Creating an external Azure Stream Analytics resource in the Azure portal is completely redundant and adds unnecessary cost. In addition, creating this external job would not solve the root problem: if the source database (DB1) is not configured to emit its changes (through CDC), no streaming engine will be able to read them, regardless of which tool you use.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to eventstreams in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Enable Extended Events for DB1. Why it is incorrect: Extended Events (XEvents) in the SQL Server and Azure SQL engine are a lightweight performance monitoring system. They are designed to help database administrators diagnose performance problems by capturing metrics such as locks, deadlocks or slow queries. They are not designed for, and do not have the capability to act as, a continuous row-level data extraction mechanism to feed real-time data engineering pipelines.

  • Official documentation: Extended Events overview - Microsoft Learn

q101.stem:
You need to recommend a solution to resolve the MAR1 connectivity issues. The solution must minimize development effort.

What should you recommend?
options: Add a ForEach activity to the data pipeline.
Configure retries for the Copy data activity.
Call a notebook from the data pipeline.
Configure Fault tolerance for the Copy data activity.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Configure retries for the Copy data activity.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option B: Configure retries for the Copy data activity. Why it is correct: The case study explicitly mentions that the team experiences "transient connectivity errors" and sets the requirement that "ingestion processes must retry the connection". Transient errors are temporary network interruptions or momentary service outages (such as the MAR1 REST API). In Microsoft Fabric, all data pipeline activities (including the Copy data activity) have built-in native properties called "Retry" and "Retry interval" on their "General" settings tab. By configuring this, the engine automatically retries the connection when it fails, resolving the connectivity problem without writing a single line of code, which strictly meets the requirement to minimize development effort.

  • Official documentation: General activity settings in pipelines (Retry property) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: Add a ForEach activity to the data pipeline. Why it is incorrect: The ForEach activity is a control structure designed to iterate or loop over a collection of items (such as a list of files, folders or tables). It has no inherent functionality to detect network failures or to apply error recovery logic or connection retries.

  • Official documentation: ForEach activity in data pipelines - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Call a notebook from the data pipeline. Why it is incorrect: Although it is technically possible to invoke an Apache Spark notebook and program a custom block of code inside it (using try-except blocks and loops in Python) to retry the connection to the MAR1 API, this would require significant programming, testing and maintenance effort. This directly violates the business requirement to "minimize development effort", especially when a native visual setting exists that does it automatically with a single click.

  • Official documentation: Notebook activity in Fabric data pipelines - Microsoft Learn

Option D: Configure Fault tolerance for the Copy data activity. Why it is incorrect: "Fault tolerance" in the Copy data activity is a very specific feature designed to ignore and skip incompatible or corrupt data rows during the copy (for example, when trying to insert text into a numeric column). It has absolutely no capability to manage or fix network-level errors, server outages or transient connectivity failures with the data source.

  • Official documentation: Fault tolerance of the copy activity in pipelines - Microsoft Learn

q102.stem:
You need to recommend a solution for handling old files. The solution must meet the technical requirements.

What should you include in the recommendation?
options: a data pipeline that includes a Copy data activity
a data pipeline that includes a Delete data activity
a notebook that runs the VACUUM command
a notebook that runs the OPTIMIZE command

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: a notebook that runs the VACUUM command

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option C: a notebook that runs the VACUUM command Why it is correct: The case study sets a very specific technical requirement: "Once a week, old files that are no longer referenced by a Delta table log must be removed". In the Delta Lake architecture (the default storage format in Fabric lakehouses), when you update or delete records, the original data files (Parquet) are not physically deleted right away, so that time travel is possible. The command designed natively to scan the transaction log, identify which files have become orphaned or outdated, and physically remove them from storage to free up space is the VACUUM command. The standard way to orchestrate this in Fabric is to run the command through Spark or SQL code in a notebook.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake table maintenance (VACUUM command) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: a data pipeline that includes a Copy data activity Why it is incorrect: The sole purpose of the Copy data activity is to move information from a source system to a destination. It has no technical capability or internal logic to read the transaction log of a Delta table, deduce which underlying Parquet files are historical or are no longer referenced, and proceed to delete them.

  • Official documentation: Copy activity in data pipelines - Microsoft Learn

Option B: a data pipeline that includes a Delete data activity Why it is incorrect: Although the Delete data activity in a pipeline is used to delete files or folders, it is a generic tool. It deletes exactly the paths that you configure rigidly. It cannot interpret Delta Lake metadata. If you try to use this activity to clean up the underlying folder of a Delta table, you run the critical risk of deleting files that are still active or transaction logs, which would corrupt the table completely.

  • Official documentation: Delete activity in data pipelines - Microsoft Learn

Option D: a notebook that runs the OPTIMIZE command Why it is incorrect: The OPTIMIZE command is designed to improve query performance by compacting small files into larger files (bin-packing) and reorganizing the data (Z-Ordering). It is important to note that when OPTIMIZE runs, the system creates new consolidated large files, but it does not automatically delete the old small files; it simply marks them as "unreferenced" in the log. Therefore, using OPTIMIZE alone will not free up physical storage space. To remove the leftovers generated by OPTIMIZE, you must then run VACUUM.

  • Official documentation: Optimizing Delta Lake tables (OPTIMIZE command) - Microsoft Learn

You have a KQL database that contains a table named Readings.

You need to build a KQL query to compare the MeterReading value of each row to the previous row base on the Timestamp value.

A sample of the expected output is shown in the following table.

How should you complete the query? To answer, drag the appropriate values the correct targets. Each value may be used once, more than once, or not at all. You may need to drag the split bar between panes or scroll to view content.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Box 1: sort

  • Box 2: extend

  • Box 3: project

Detailed analysis of the correct sequence

Box 1: sort Why it is correct: For row-based window functions such as prev() (which looks up the value of the immediately preceding row) to work logically and predictably, the dataset must be serialized or sorted chronologically. The sort operator (which is a synonym of order in KQL) arranges the rows based on the specified column (Timestamp), establishing the sequential order needed to make the comparison.

  • Official documentation: sort operator in KQL - Microsoft Learn

Box 2: extend Why it is correct: The goal in this step is to calculate the previous values and add them as new data fields, without losing the original columns of the table (such as City, Area, etc.). The extend operator is designed for exactly this purpose: it evaluates the expressions provided (in this case, prev(MeterReading) and prev(Timestamp)) and appends those new calculated columns to the existing result set.

  • Official documentation: extend operator in KQL - Microsoft Learn

Box 3: project Why it is correct: The final step of the query must format the output so that it matches exactly the columns and order shown in the sample table in the problem. The project operator explicitly selects which columns to keep in the final result set, discarding any other temporary or unwanted columns that may exist in the original table, and presenting them in the exact order in which they are declared.

  • Official documentation: project operator in KQL - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

evaluate: Why it is incorrect: The evaluate operator is used to invoke built-in tabular query plugins, such as creating pivot tables, unpacking JSON objects or advanced time series analysis. It is not a valid command for basic sorting, column creation or projection selection operations.

  • Official documentation: evaluate operator in KQL - Microsoft Learn

lookup: Why it is incorrect: The lookup operator extends the columns of a fact table with values looked up in a dimension table, working similarly to a left join. Since the query in this scenario runs entirely over a single table (Readings) to compare rows with each other, there is no second table to look up external data from.

  • Official documentation: lookup operator in KQL - Microsoft Learn

summarize: Why it is incorrect: The summarize operator is used to perform groupings and mathematical aggregations (such as sums, averages or counts) over a dataset. If you used this command, the individual rows would be merged into groups, destroying the sequential row structure needed to compare a chronological reading with the previous one.

  • Official documentation: summarize operator in KQL - Microsoft Learn

take: Why it is incorrect: The take command (or limit) simply restricts the number of rows returned by the query (for example, returning only 10 arbitrary rows). It has no functionality for sorting the data by date, creating calculated columns or selecting the final output format of the columns.

  • Official documentation: take operator in KQL - Microsoft Learn
