You need to recommend a Fabric streaming solution that will use the sources shown in the following table.

The solution must minimize development effort.

What should you include in the recommendation for each source? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Source 1: An eventstream

  • Source 2 A streaming dataflow

  • Source 3: Apache Spark Structured Streaming

Detailed analysis of the correct sequence

Dropdown 1 (Source1): An eventstream Why it is correct: The description indicates that the messages contain semi-structured data and a column of type bigint. In the Microsoft ecosystem, the "Streaming dataflow" tool has a strict, documented technical limitation: it does not support the bigint data type. Since the goal is to minimize development effort, you should rule out using complex Spark code if a visual tool exists. A Fabric "eventstream" is a no-code solution that handles semi-structured data (such as JSON) perfectly and supports large data types (bigint) when routing them natively to KQL databases, meeting all the requirements with minimal effort.

  • Official documentation: Streaming dataflow limitations (no BigInt support) - Microsoft Learn

Dropdown 2 (Source2): A streaming dataflow Why it is correct: This source contains traditional tabular structured data (19 columns). The "Streaming dataflow" tool is built on the Power Query visual engine and is designed specifically to connect to, ingest and transform strongly structured data in real time through a drag-and-drop graphical interface. This absolutely minimizes development effort compared with writing Spark scripts to flatten and type columns.

  • Official documentation: Create and use streaming dataflows for structured data - Microsoft Learn

Dropdown 3 (Source3): Apache Spark Structured Streaming Why it is correct: The description specifies that the messages contain unstructured data, specifically images. None of the visual low-code tools in Fabric (neither an eventstream nor a streaming dataflow) can natively ingest, parse or process binary image payloads. The only streaming solution in Fabric capable of connecting to a source, reading binary files or images in a continuous stream and processing them is Apache Spark Structured Streaming, which makes it the only technically viable option.

  • Official documentation: Processing unstructured data and images with Spark Structured Streaming - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

A data pipeline: Why it is incorrect: A data pipeline is an orchestration tool designed for batch data processing and movement (batch ETL), not for continuous real-time streaming scenarios. Since the question explicitly requires you to "recommend a streaming solution", this option is ruled out for any of the three sources.

  • Official documentation: Data pipeline basics versus real-time streams - Microsoft Learn

The "Message size" distractor: It is important to note that, although the message size column shows values of 10 MB, 25 MB and 5 MB (which technically exceed the standard 1 MB limit of Event Hubs/eventstreams), in the logic of the Microsoft Data Engineering certifications, the descriptive details about the data types (bigint, structured, images) are the main keys that define which tool to use. If you relied exclusively on size and ignored the descriptions, you would have to use Spark for all three, which would violate the mandatory instruction to "minimize development effort" by using low-code tools where the structure of the data allows it.

Here is the detailed analysis of the incorrect options for Question 104, broken down by source and with their respective links to the official Microsoft documentation, ensuring compliance with the prohibition on using italic characters.

Analysis of the incorrect options for Source 1

The requirement is: Semi-structured data with a bigint column. (Correct answer: An eventstream).

A streaming dataflow: Why it is incorrect: The streaming dataflow engine (inherited from Power BI) has a strict data type limitation and does not support the bigint type. If you try to use it, large numeric data will fail to load or will be truncated.

  • Official documentation: Streaming dataflow limitations (no BigInt support) - Microsoft Learn

Apache Spark Structured Streaming: Why it is incorrect: It requires provisioning a cluster and writing code manually (in Python, Scala or SQL). This directly violates the case study rule of minimizing development effort, since an eventstream can do the job through a no-code graphical interface.

  • Official documentation: Apache Spark Structured Streaming in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

A data pipeline: Why it is incorrect: Data pipelines are batch data orchestration tools (batch ETL), not real-time stream processing tools.

  • Official documentation: Data pipeline basics - Microsoft Learn

Analysis of the incorrect options for Source 2

The requirement is: Structured data with 19 columns. (Correct answer: A streaming dataflow).

An eventstream: Why it is incorrect: Although it can ingest continuous data, it lacks a robust visual tabular data transformation engine (Power Query). To flatten, clean or change data types in a rigid 19-column structure visually and with minimal effort, the right tool is the streaming dataflow.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to eventstreams and their transformations - Microsoft Learn

Apache Spark Structured Streaming: Why it is incorrect: Using Spark requires programming the schema structure (schema inference) and the transformations of those 19 columns through code. This takes much more development effort than using the Power Query graphical visual interface.

  • Official documentation: DataFrame operations in Spark Structured Streaming - Microsoft Learn

A data pipeline: Why it is incorrect: Again, it does not meet the main requirement of being a streaming solution; it is an orchestrator for scheduled batch data loads.

  • Official documentation: Choosing between dataflows and data pipelines - Microsoft Learn

Analysis of the incorrect options for Source 3

The requirement is: Unstructured data that contains images. (Correct answer: Apache Spark Structured Streaming).

An eventstream: Why it is incorrect: The eventstream visual tool is designed to work with telemetry and text messages (such as JSON or CSV). It has no native capability to ingest, decode or process completely unstructured binary file payloads such as images.

  • Official documentation: Supported data formats in eventstreams - Microsoft Learn

A streaming dataflow: Why it is incorrect: Its tabular engine is designed for structured (tabular) or basic semi-structured data. It cannot process images or manipulate unstructured binary payloads in real time.

  • Official documentation: Supported data types and sources in streaming dataflows - Microsoft Learn

A data pipeline: Why it is incorrect: It is a bulk batch data movement tool. Although it can move image files from one folder to another, it is not a continuous stream processing (streaming) tool, failing the basic requirement of the question.

  • Official documentation: Supported activities in data pipelines - Microsoft Learn

q105.stem: What should you do to optimize the query experience for the business users?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Enable V-Order.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option A: Enable V-Order. Why it is correct: In Microsoft exam case studies, you must always look for the explicit clues planted in the environment description. The text literally says: "The gold layer is in a warehouse where V-Order is disabled".

V-Order is a write optimization technology exclusive to Microsoft Fabric that is applied to Parquet-format files. Its main function is to sort, compress and structure the data in such a way that compute engines (such as the SQL endpoint or the Power BI engine) can perform reads at ultra-fast speeds in memory. With this feature disabled in the gold layer (the final layer that business users query), the performance of ad hoc queries and reports is severely degraded, causing the two-hour load times and the timeout errors ("The SQL query failed"). Enabling V-Order is the direct architectural action to resolve this bottleneck.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake table optimization and V-Order in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option B: Create and update statistics. Why it is incorrect: Although in traditional SQL Server engines creating and updating statistics is vital for the query optimizer to choose the best execution plan, in the Microsoft Fabric environment (especially in Delta Parquet columnar storage) the physical optimization of the files is the most critical performance factor. In addition, Fabric generates statistics automatically in many operations. The explicit mention that V-Order is disabled indicates that the performance problem is about physical access and data decompression, not a problem of execution plans caused by missing statistics.

  • Official documentation: Statistics in Fabric data warehousing - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Run the VACUUM command. Why it is incorrect: The VACUUM command is a storage maintenance tool. Its function is to read the transaction log of a Delta table and physically delete the old data files that are no longer referenced by the current version of the table. Although it frees up disk space and helps with storage costs, it does not reorder the active data nor substantially improve the speed at which the SQL engine reads the current records during a heavy analytical query.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake table maintenance (VACUUM command) - Microsoft Learn

Option D: Introduce primary keys. Why it is incorrect: Assuming this is a poor automated translation of "Primary Keys", in the Fabric warehouse, primary key and foreign key constraints are "non-enforced". They serve only as informational metadata. Although they can help the engine slightly to understand the relationships, they do not solve a bulk read query performance problem as serious as the one caused by having V-Order compression disabled in the final consumption layer.

  • Official documentation: Table constraints in Microsoft Fabric data warehousing - Microsoft Learn

q106.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a warehouse named Warehouse1.

While monitoring Warehouse1, you discover that query performance has degraded during the last 60 minutes.

You need to isolate all the queries that were run during the last 60 minutes. The results must include the username of the users that submitted the queries and the query statements.

What should you use?
options: the Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: views from the queryinsights schema

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option B: views from the queryinsights schema Why it is correct: In the Microsoft Fabric warehouse, the system automatically captures the query execution history and makes it available to users through the system views in the queryinsights schema. Specifically, the queryinsights.exec_requests_history view stores detailed information about recently completed queries, including the command column (the full SQL query statement), the login_name column (the name of the user who ran it) and the start and end timestamps. This lets you filter with mathematical precision everything that ran in the last 60 minutes to isolate the performance problem.

  • Official documentation: Query insights in Fabric data warehousing - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: the Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app Why it is incorrect: The Capacity Metrics app is a high-level monitoring tool designed for administrators to track Capacity Unit (CU) consumption, billing and resource throttling at the level of the whole workspace or capacity. It is not designed for granular analysis at the level of individual SQL query code, nor does it provide the exact text of T-SQL statements cross-referenced with the user name in a queryable way for debugging.

  • Official documentation: What is the Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Query activity Why it is incorrect: Although the Fabric Monitoring hub lets you see some item "activity", it does not provide a SQL-based relational view that lets you cross-reference the execution history, the exact text of T-SQL queries and the user names with the flexibility needed to diagnose specific performance drops in the last 60 minutes. The queryinsights schema is the technical feature built expressly for this kind of auditing in the warehouse.

  • Official documentation: Workspace monitoring in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option D: the sys.dm_exec_requests dynamic management view Why it is incorrect: Dynamic management views (DMVs) such as sys.dm_exec_requests show only the queries that are running at the exact moment you run the query (real-time or active). Once a query finishes, it immediately disappears from this view. Therefore, it is impossible to use it to isolate the history of queries that already finished during the last 60 minutes.

  • Official documentation: sys.dm_exec_requests (Transact-SQL) - Microsoft Learn

You have a Fabric workspace that contains a semantic model named Model1.

You need to monitor the refresh history of Model1 and visualize the refresh history in a chart.

What should you use?
options: the refresh history from the settings of Model1

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: a notebook

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option B: a notebook Why it is correct: The main requirement demands two actions: monitoring the history and "visualizing it in a chart". The default graphical interface of semantic models does not offer analytical charts of their refresh times. To achieve this in Microsoft Fabric, the right tool is a notebook using the native Semantic Link (sempy) library. By using Python code, you can extract the refresh history directly into a DataFrame by using functions such as list_refresh_history() and, in the same cell, use standard libraries such as Matplotlib or Seaborn to render custom visual charts of execution times, durations or failures.

  • Official documentation: Use Semantic Link to extract semantic model metadata in notebooks - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: the refresh history from the settings of Model1 Why it is incorrect: If you navigate to the settings of a semantic model in the Fabric workspace, you can access a log called "Refresh history". However, this interface presents the information exclusively as a flat table or list of records in text format (showing the status, the start and end time). It has no built-in functionality to generate, draw or visualize that data in a chart.

  • Official documentation: Viewing the refresh history of semantic models - Microsoft Learn

Option C: a Dataflow Gen2 dataflow Why it is incorrect: A Dataflow Gen2 is a data transformation engine based on Power Query (visual ETL). Its purpose is to connect to external sources, clean the data and load it into a destination (such as a lakehouse). It is not designed to read the internal metadata or administration logs of Fabric semantic models, nor is it a visualization or analytical charting tool.

Option D: a data pipeline Why it is incorrect: Data pipelines are logical task orchestration tools. Although you can configure an activity in a pipeline to "trigger" or force the refresh of a semantic model, the pipeline itself is not a visualization engine nor does it have a canvas to plot charts, boxes or visual reports about the historical behavior of those models.

q108.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a write-intensive warehouse named DW1. DW1 stores staging tables that are used to load a dimensional model. The tables are often read once, dropped, and then recreated to process new data.

You need to minimize the load time of DW1.

What should you do?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Disable V-Order.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option D: Disable V-Order. Why it is correct: In the Microsoft Fabric architecture, V-Order is a storage optimization that applies advanced sorting and compression to Parquet files at the moment they are written. This process consumes CPU resources and adds extra time during the write (load) phase. The case study describes a classic scenario of staging tables, which are read-once, short-lived and write-intensive workloads. For this specific pattern, Microsoft explicitly recommends disabling V-Order. By doing so, you remove the compression time penalty during the write, making the bulk load time of the data as fast as possible.

  • Official documentation: When to disable V-Order on warehouse tables - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: Enable V-Order. Why it is incorrect: Enabling V-Order would produce exactly the opposite of the desired effect. Sorting and compressing the data dictionaries takes compute processing time. Applying this optimization to transient tables that are read only once and then destroyed is a waste of resources that will significantly slow down the load (ingestion) speed into the warehouse.

  • Official documentation: V-Order write behavior - Microsoft Learn

Option B: Create statistics. Why it is incorrect: Creating statistics means the database engine must scan the rows of the newly loaded tables to build histograms on the data distribution. This scanning process requires additional processing and time, which would increase the total duration of the load window. Also, investing time in creating detailed statistics for ephemeral tables that will be deleted right after their first use makes no architectural sense.

  • Official documentation: Performance considerations for statistics in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Drop statistics. Why it is incorrect: (Note: This option corresponds to the DROP STATISTICS command.) Dropping existing statistics is not the main or appropriate mechanism for speeding up the physical bulk loading of data into Fabric warehouse tables. Since the case study states that the tables are dropped and recreated entirely to process new data, any associated statistics would be removed along with the table anyway, so running this command does not reduce ingestion time.

  • Official documentation: Manage statistics in the data warehouse - Microsoft Learn

You have a Fabric deployment pipeline that uses three workspaces named Dev, Test, and Prod.

You need to deploy an Eventhouse as part of the deployment process.

What should you use to add the Eventhouse to the deployment process?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: An Azure DevOps pipeline

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option A: An Azure DevOps pipeline Why it is correct (scenario specifics): As we have analyzed, this question has a peculiarity found in simulators: it omits the ideal native answer from the list of options. Given this situation, the only architecturally viable and functional solution is to use an Azure DevOps pipeline. Microsoft Fabric has a deep, native integration with Azure Repos. When the deployment process requires advanced automation or the built-in visual tool is not enough, the practice recommended by Microsoft for Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) is to connect the workspace to Azure DevOps. From there, you can use an Azure DevOps pipeline that consumes the Fabric REST APIs to promote and deploy items, such as an eventhouse, across the Dev, Test and Prod environments in an automated and secure way.

  • Official documentation: Git integration and CI/CD automation with Azure DevOps in Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option B: An eventstream Why it is incorrect: Technically, an eventstream is a real-time telemetry ingestion and processing engine. Its sole purpose is to capture continuous messages and route them to storage destinations, such as a KQL database within an eventhouse. It has absolutely no orchestration, source control or schema promotion capability, so it cannot be used as a mechanism for deploying infrastructure across different environments.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to eventstreams in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option C: GitHub Actions Why it is incorrect: Although Microsoft Fabric supports integration with GitHub repositories, Azure DevOps is Microsoft's first-party platform. In the context of official certifications, when a continuous deployment business scenario backed by Microsoft Entra ID is presented and you must choose between Azure DevOps and GitHub without the question stating an explicit open-source requirement, the native solution recommended and preferred by the Microsoft ecosystem is Azure DevOps.

q110.stem:
You have a Fabric warehouse named DW1. DW1 contains a table that stores sales data and is used by multiple sales representatives.

You plan to implement row-level security (RLS).

You need to ensure that the sales representatives can see only their respective data.

Which warehouse object do you require to implement RLS?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: FUNCTION

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option C: FUNCTION Why it is correct: In a Microsoft Fabric warehouse, as in SQL Server, row-level security (RLS) is implemented by creating a security predicate. This predicate must be defined by writing an inline table-valued function. This function contains the filtering logic based on identity (for example, evaluating whether the sales representative's name in the row matches the user running the query through system functions such as USER_NAME()). This function is then bound to the table through a security policy, which applies the filter invisibly on every query.

  • Official documentation: Row-level security in Fabric data warehousing - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: TRIGGER Why it is incorrect: Triggers are objects designed to run code automatically in reaction to data modification events (such as INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE). They are not architecturally designed to intercept read statements (SELECT) or to apply security filters to user queries. Also, in the current architecture of the Microsoft Fabric warehouse, traditional DML triggers are not supported.

  • Official documentation: T-SQL surface area supported in Microsoft Fabric (Limitations) - Microsoft Learn

Option B: SCHEMA Why it is incorrect: Although it is an excellent security practice to create a separate schema (for example, a schema named Security) to hold the RLS objects and restrict who can modify them, a schema is simply a logical container or organizational folder. By itself, a schema has no ability to evaluate logical conditions or to filter the sales data dynamically.

  • Official documentation: Best practices for implementing row-level security - Microsoft Learn

Option D: DATABASE ROLE Why it is incorrect: Database roles are used for object-level access control. They are used to grant broad permissions (for example, allowing the group of sales representatives to run a SELECT command on the whole table). However, a database role cannot dynamically filter the internal content of that table so that Representative 1 sees Row 1 and Representative 2 sees Row 2. To achieve that granularity, the user's identity or their role membership must be evaluated within the logic of an RLS function.

  • Official documentation: Security in Microsoft Fabric data warehousing (Roles versus RLS) - Microsoft Learn

q111.stem:
You have a Fabric warehouse named DW1. DW1 contains a table that stores sales data and is used by multiple sales representatives.

You plan to implement row-level security (RLS).

You need to ensure that the sales representatives can see only their respective data.

Which warehouse object do you require to implement RLS?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: SECURITY POLICY

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option A: SECURITY POLICY Why it is correct: This question is a direct variation of question 110. To fully implement row-level security (RLS) in the Microsoft Fabric SQL engine, the architecture requires two fundamental objects: the function (which contains the logic) and the security policy. The security policy is the definitive database object that binds the filter function to the actual sales table. Without creating this security policy object, the predicate function is useless, because it is the policy that tells the core Fabric engine to intercept any incoming query and apply the filter invisibly so that each representative sees only their own data.

  • Official documentation: Row-level security in Fabric data warehousing (Creating security policies) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option B: TABLE Why it is incorrect: A table is simply the physical storage object where the sales data resides. A table by itself is a passive object; it has no internal logic engine capable of detecting which user is querying it in order to dynamically hide its own rows. To protect it, you need to layer the security policy object on top.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Fabric data warehousing - Microsoft Learn

Option C: TRIGGER Why it is incorrect: As we explained in the previous question, triggers are reactive objects that fire after a data modification event (insert, update, delete). They cannot intercept read statements (SELECT) to mask or hide rows from a user, and in fact the current architecture of the Fabric warehouse does not support traditional transactional triggers.

  • Official documentation: T-SQL surface area supported in Microsoft Fabric (Limitations) - Microsoft Learn

Option D: STORED PROCEDURE Why it is incorrect: A stored procedure is a block of code that groups SQL statements. You could write one that includes a filter (WHERE clause) based on the user, but this is not a true centralized RLS architecture. If the user bypasses the procedure and connects a Power BI report directly to the table, they would have access to all of the company's data, breaking security. The security policy is enforced at the engine level, so it protects the data regardless of how or from where the sales representative tries to access it.

q112.stem:
You have a Fabric F32 capacity that contains a workspace. The workspace contains a warehouse named DW1 that is modelled by using MD5 hash surrogate keys.

DW1 contains a single fact table that has grown from 200 million rows to 500 million rows during the past year.

You have Microsoft Power BI reports that are based on Direct Lake. The reports show year-over-year values.

Users report that the performance of some of the reports has degraded over time and some visuals show errors.

You need to resolve the performance issues. The solution must meet the following requirements:

• Provide the best query performance.

• Minimize operational costs.

Which should you do?
options: Modify the surrogate keys to use a different data type.
Change the MD5 hash to SHA256.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Increase the capacity.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option: Increase the capacity.

  • Why it is correct: As the official Microsoft Fabric documentation shows, Direct Lake mode operates under strict architectural limits defined by the SKU tier in order to maintain optimal in-memory performance. An F32 capacity has a hard, non-negotiable limit of 300 million rows per table. Since the fact table in the scenario has grown to 500 million rows, it has completely exceeded this hardware limit. When this happens, the Power BI engine performs a fallback (automatic fallback) to DirectQuery, which explains the severe performance drop and the visual timeout errors. To meet the requirement to "provide the best query performance", it is mandatory to restore Direct Lake operation. The only technical solution that lets the engine support 500 million rows in memory is to increase the capacity to the next tier (F64, which supports up to 1.5 billion rows). The requirement to "minimize operational costs" is respected by scaling only to F64 (the minimum necessary) instead of oversizing the infrastructure.

  • Official documentation: Direct Lake memory limits and scaling for Power BI and Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option: Modify the surrogate keys to use a different data type.

  • Why it is incorrect: Replacing text strings (MD5 hashes) with a numeric data type (such as BIGINT) is one of the best dimensional modeling practices for reducing the size of in-memory dictionaries. However, in this specific case, changing the data type does not reduce the number of rows. The table will still have 500 million records, so it will continue to exceed the strict 300 million row limit of the F32 capacity and fall back to the slow DirectQuery mode.

  • Official documentation: Modeling guidelines: Numeric data types versus strings - Microsoft Learn

Option: Disable V-Order on the warehouse.

  • Why it is incorrect: V-Order is Fabric's native algorithm that sorts, compresses and optimizes the reading of Delta Parquet files at the storage level. Disabling it would remove this fundamental optimization, making disk scans drastically slower. This would achieve exactly the opposite of "provide the best query performance".

  • Official documentation: Delta table optimization and V-Order in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option: Change the MD5 hash to SHA256.

  • Why it is incorrect: A SHA256 hash (256 bits) takes up twice the storage and memory of an MD5 hash (128 bits). Migrating to SHA256 would inflate the text dictionaries in the VertiPaq engine even further, worsening the memory overflow and sinking the reports even more abruptly.

  • Official documentation: Dimensional modeling and performance considerations - Microsoft Learn

Option: Create views.

  • Why it is incorrect: Creating views (VIEWS) in a warehouse only adds a logical query layer on top of the base data. Views do not compress the information, do not change the underlying model and, most importantly, do not remove the fact that the Direct Lake engine has to deal with 500 million physical rows exceeding the capacity of the F32 SKU.

You plan to deploy Warehouse 1 to a new workspace named Workspace2.

As part of the deployment process, you need to verify whether Warehouse1 contains invalid references. The solution must minimize development effort and provide detailed information about the invalid references.

Option D: A database project

All of this happens natively, perfectly meeting the requirement to minimize development effort (zero manual code).

Option: A dbt project

Option: A Python script

However, having to design, code, test and maintain that code from scratch requires a lot of development effort, which fails the main requirement of the question.

q114.stem:
HOTSPOT

-

You are building a data loading pattern for Fabric notebook workloads.

You have the following code segment.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true.

Otherwise, select No.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Statement 1 (The target table will always be overwritten): No

  • Statement 2 (The merge operation will always run): No

  • Statement 3 (The code supports incremental loading and the initial table creation): Yes

Detailed analysis of the statements

Statement 1: The target table will always be overwritten (No) Why this answer is correct: If you analyze the structure of the Python code, the write statement with overwrite mode (mode overwrite) is nested exclusively inside the first except Exception block. In Python's error-handling logic, this except block only fires if the statement in the preceding try block fails. That preceding statement tries to read the existing Delta table. Therefore, the table is only overwritten (or created) if it did not previously exist. If the table already exists, the read succeeds, the except block is skipped entirely and the data is not overwritten, moving directly to the merge logic.

  • Official documentation: Exception handling in Python for Spark data flows - Microsoft Learn

Statement 2: The merge operation will always run (No) Why this answer is correct: The key detail of this code segment is the return statement located at the end of the first except Exception block. If the table does not exist, the code enters that except block, creates the table by using saveAsTable and then executes that return. The return command immediately ends the execution of the function. This means the interpreter exits the script and never reaches the lower line where the merge_operation is defined and executed. The merge only runs when the table already exists (the first try succeeds and the except's return is not triggered).

  • Official documentation: Merge operations in Delta Lake on Apache Spark - Microsoft Learn

Statement 3: The code supports incremental loading and the initial table creation (Yes) Why this answer is correct: This script implements a classic data engineering pattern known as a robust UPSERT.

  1. Initial creation: It is handled in the except block. If it is the first time the notebook runs and the table does not exist, the system creates it from scratch from the source DataFrame.

  2. Incremental load: It is handled in the second try block. In later runs (when the table already exists), the code dynamically compares the candidate keys, inserts the new records (whenNotMatchedInsertAll) and updates the records that have changed (whenMatchedUpdate). This is exactly what defines an incremental load process.

  • Official documentation: Initial and incremental data loading strategies in Delta Lake - Microsoft Learn

q115.stem:
You have an Azure event hub. Each event contains the following fields:

• BikepointID

• Street

• Neighbourhood

• Latitude

• Longitude

• No_Bikes

• No_Empty_Docks

You need to ingest the events. The solution must only retain events that have a Neighbourhood value of Chelsea, and then store the retained events in a Fabric lakehouse.

Data retention in case of failure is required to be two days.

What should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: An eventstream

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option A: An eventstream Why it is correct: In Microsoft Fabric, an eventstream is the native tool designed to capture, transform and route real-time data without writing code. It perfectly meets the three requirements of the scenario:

  1. Ingestion: It lets you configure a native source by connecting directly to the Azure event hub.

  2. Filtering: It includes a built-in visual processor called Filter, where you can configure a simple rule to let through only the events where the Neighbourhood column equals Chelsea, discarding the rest before sending them to the lakehouse.

  3. Retention: Fabric eventstreams have a native, service-managed data retention setting. You can configure this retention to exactly two days. If the destination lakehouse suffers an outage or error, the eventstream will internally retain those messages for that period, ensuring that no information is lost and allowing it to be ingested once the destination is available again.

  • Official documentation: Configure data retention in Fabric eventstreams - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option B: Apache Spark Structured Streaming Why it is incorrect: Although Spark Structured Streaming can connect to an event hub, filter the data through code and write it to a lakehouse, it does not efficiently meet the internal retention requirement. Spark handles fault tolerance through checkpoints, but it does not temporarily store the data in its own buffer for two days; it depends entirely on the retention settings of the source. Also, it requires development effort through programming, whereas an eventstream offers the same solution natively and visually.

  • Official documentation: Fault tolerance with checkpoints in Spark Structured Streaming - Microsoft Learn

Option C: A streaming dataset Why it is incorrect: A streaming dataset is a legacy Power BI feature designed to push data directly to a real-time visual dashboard or scorecard. It has no architectural capability to process transformations, filter records, or route physical data to be stored permanently in a lakehouse in Delta Parquet format. It also has no configurable retention buffer for fault tolerance.

  • Official documentation: Real-time streaming datasets in Power BI - Microsoft Learn

Option D: a KQL queryset Why it is incorrect: A KQL queryset is strictly an analytical consumption tool. It is used to write and run queries over data that has already been ingested and stored in a KQL database. It is not a data ingestion engine, it cannot connect to an external source such as Azure Event Hubs to pull data, and it cannot be used to save information to a lakehouse.

  • Official documentation: Use KQL querysets in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the statements

Statement 1: Line 01 will replace all null and empty values (No) Why this answer is correct: In PySpark, a null value (the total absence of data, or NULL) is fundamentally different from an empty value (a text string with no characters such as ""). The logical condition written in Line 01 uses the isNull() function. This function strictly and exclusively evaluates null values. If a row contains an empty value (empty string), the isNull() condition will return false and the empty value will remain intact, not being replaced by the word "Unknown". To catch both cases, an additional condition checking whether the string length is zero would be required.

  • Official documentation: isNull function in Apache Spark - Microsoft Learn

Statement 2: Line 02 will extract the value before the first period (No) Why this answer is correct: When you use the split() function in PySpark, the result is an array of elements. Arrays in PySpark are indexed starting from zero. If we look at the sample email in the table (dennis.awkland@fabric.io) and split it on the period, we get an array where "dennis" is position 0 and "awkland@fabric" is position 1. Line 02 of the code uses getItem(1), which extracts the second element ("awkland@fabric"), that is, the value after the first period, not the one before it. To extract the value before the first period, the code would need to use getItem(0).

  • Official documentation: split function in Apache Spark - Microsoft Learn

Statement 3: Line 03 will extract the year value from the OrderDate column and name it Year (Yes) Why this answer is correct: Line 03 of the code correctly uses the native year("OrderDate") function. This Spark date-processing function is designed specifically to numerically extract the year component of a date or timestamp column. Immediately afterward, the code chains the .alias("Year") method, which is the standard PySpark command for dynamically renaming the result of a function within a select statement. Therefore, the statement's description matches the code execution exactly.

You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains three notebooks named notebook_01, notebook_02, and notebook_03.

You are building a new notebook in Workspace1 that will contain the following Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) definition.

You need to modify the DAG definition to meet the following requirements:

• Ensure that notebook_01 and notebook_02 run in parallel.

• Ensure that notebook_02 only runs after the execution of notebook_03 is complete.

How should you modify the DAG definition?
options: Create a second DAG definition. Move notebook_03 and notebook_02 to the new DAG definition.
Move the notebook_03 declaration to the top of the DAG definition. Add a concurrency to notebook_02 and notebook_01.
Create two stages in the DAG definition. Add notebook_03 to the first stage. Add notebook_01 and notebook_02 to the second stage.
Move the declaration of notebook_03 to the top of the DAG definition. Add a new stage that contains notebook_01 and notebook_02.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Create two stages in the DAG definition. Add notebook_03 to the first stage. Add notebook_01 and notebook_02 to the second stage.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option C: Create two stages in the DAG definition... Why it is correct: In the Python API for the mssparkutils.notebook.runMultiple() utility, the execution flow is controlled through a graph topology (DAG). Although at the JSON code level there is no literal property called "stage", in the architectural context of this Microsoft exam the term stage is used conceptually to define the topological dependency levels.

To meet the business requirements, the DAG topology must be logically configured in two dependency levels:

  1. First stage: Contains only notebook_03. At the code level, this JSON block would have no declared dependency, so the Spark engine runs it immediately when the process starts.

  2. Second stage: Contains notebook_01 and notebook_02. At the code level, both blocks would include the dependencies property pointing to the previous notebook (for example: "dependencies": ["run_notebook_3"]).

Because they share exactly the same dependency and do not depend on each other, the Fabric orchestration engine natively guarantees that notebook_01 and notebook_02 will start at the same time (in parallel) and only once the execution of notebook_03 has finished.

  • Official documentation: Microsoft Spark Utilities (MSSparkUtils) for Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option B and Option D: Move the declaration to the top of the DAG definition... Why they are incorrect: The vertical order in which the text blocks are written inside the activities array is completely irrelevant to the execution engine. The runMultiple function ignores the top-to-bottom reading order and builds the execution order purely and exclusively from the dependency properties declared inside each block. Therefore, moving the notebook_03 code to the top of the script will not force the orchestrator to run it first.

  • Official documentation: Orchestrating and running notebooks in parallel - Microsoft Learn

Option A: Create a second DAG definition. Move notebook_03 and notebook_02 to the new DAG definition. Why it is incorrect: Splitting the code into two different JSON dictionary variables would force you to run two completely independent runMultiple commands in the main notebook. Although this would force a separation, it is a bad data engineering practice. Splitting the orchestration breaks the engine's ability to dynamically optimize the shared resources of the Spark cluster in a single unified session, prevents notebook_01 and notebook_02 from running in parallel under the same monitoring umbrella, and loses the ability to view the complete execution diagram in a single visual graph.

  • Official documentation: Spark performance and monitoring best practices - Microsoft Learn

Therefore, the Admin role is the only valid option available to meet the user management requirement.

  • Official documentation: Roles in Microsoft Fabric workspaces and their permissions - Microsoft Learn

To Group2: Configure only item security for Workspace2. Why it is correct: The principle of least privilege requires that Group2 have access only to the HR and Legal warehouses, excluding everything else. The Fabric security model is hierarchical: if you assigned any workspace-level role in Workspace2 (even Viewer), the users would automatically inherit read access to the reports that also reside in that same workspace. The only architectural way to isolate access to specific items (such as a warehouse) within a single workspace is to grant no permissions at the general container level and instead share the individual items directly (item-level security).

  • Official documentation: Item sharing and direct permissions in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

To User1: Assign the Contributor role for Workspace2 and the Viewer role for Workspace4. Why it is correct: User1 needs to read the Operations reports that are isolated in Workspace4; for this, the Viewer role is perfect and meets least privilege. As for Workspace2 (HR and Legal), the user needs to read the content and also create new items. The Contributor role is designed for exactly this: it grants the ability to create, edit and delete content within the workspace without granting excessive administrative permissions that would violate data governance policies.

  • Official documentation: Comparison of capabilities and permissions by workspace role - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

For Group1:

Options: Assign the Contributor / Viewer role for Workspace1. Why they are incorrect: Neither of these two roles has the permissions required in the Fabric API to add new users or manage workspace security. Assigning them would block the finance team, preventing them from meeting the explicit requirement in the question.

  • Official documentation: Limitations of the Contributor and Viewer roles - Microsoft Learn

For Group2:

Options: Assign the Viewer / Contributor role for Workspace2. Why they are incorrect: By assigning permissions directly on the workspace container, Fabric inheritance would let Group2 view (and even edit, in the case of Contributor) the HR and Legal reports. This directly breaks the business rule that requires access "only to the warehouse".

  • Official documentation: Permission inheritance and workspace-level security - Microsoft Learn

For User1:

Option: Assign the Member role for Workspace2 and the Viewer role for Workspace4. Why it is incorrect: Although this configuration would let User1 create items, it flatly violates the case study requirement to follow the principle of least privilege. The Member role includes secondary administrative privileges, such as updating the workspace app or sharing items, capabilities that were not requested for this user. The Contributor role is the exact boundary needed.

  • Official documentation: Applying the principle of least privilege in Fabric workspaces - Microsoft Learn

Option: Assign the Viewer role for Workspace2 and the Contributor role for Workspace4. Why it is incorrect: This option reverses the requested roles. It would leave User1 blocked, unable to create new items in Workspace2 (which is where the business requires it) and would grant excessive edit permissions in Workspace4 (where the user should only be able to read).

  • Official documentation: Planning workspace access - Microsoft Learn

q127.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that is connected to a GitHub repository named repo1. Workspace1 contains the items shown in the following table.

You modify Semanticmodel1, Semanticmodel2, and Report2.

You need to commit the changes to repo1.

What is the minimum number of commits you should perform?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 1

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option A: 1 Why it is correct: In Git version control integration in Microsoft Fabric, when you make changes to one or more items within the same workspace (in this case, two semantic models and a report), the source control interface groups all the selected modified items into a single list of pending changes. When you select the Commit button, the system packages and sends all the selected items in a single commit operation to the GitHub repository branch. Therefore, the minimum number of commits needed to record the changes of these three items at the same time is exactly 1.

  • Official documentation: Get started with Git integration in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option B: 2, Option C: 3, Option D: 4 Why they are incorrect: There is no technical requirement in the Fabric Git synchronization architecture that forces changes to be separated by item type, or that limits commits to a single item per commit. Although the interface lets you select or deselect items granularly in the source control panel, the standard practice and the minimum number required to push multiple concurrent changes is to group them all in a single unified commit. Requiring multiple commits for the same batch of changes would add unnecessary fragmentation to the repository history.

  • Official documentation: Git integration process - Microsoft Learn

q128.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1.

Lakehouse1 contains a table named Table1.

You need to ensure that a user named User1 can view only specific rows in Table1.

What should you do first?
options: Grant User1 the SELECT permission for Table1.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Create a function.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option B: Create a function Why it is correct: In Microsoft Fabric, to implement row-level security (RLS) on Delta tables in a lakehouse (or in its SQL analytics endpoint), the first mandatory architectural step is to write an inline table-valued function. This function contains the filtering logic that determines which rows User1 can see (for example, by evaluating user functions such as USER_NAME()). None of the other objects (such as the security policy or the predicate) can exist or be configured unless this function, which acts as the logical basis of the filtering, has been created beforehand.

  • Official documentation: Row-level security in Fabric data warehousing - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: Create a security predicate. Why it is incorrect: The security predicate is not an independent object that is created in isolation as the first step; the predicate is defined inside the inline table-valued function or applied through the security policy. Therefore, conceptually the indispensable previous step is creating the function.

  • Official documentation: Implementing RLS using security predicates - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Create a security policy. Why it is incorrect: The security policy is the definitive database object that binds the filter function to the physical table. If you try to create the security policy first, it fails immediately because the function that it must associate as a predicate has not been created yet.

  • Official documentation: Creating security policies - Microsoft Learn

Option D: Grant User1 the SELECT permission for Table1. Why it is incorrect: Granting read (SELECT) permissions on the table before implementing row-level security would give User1 unrestricted access to all the rows of Table1, failing the security requirement. Base object permissions are managed independently from the dynamic row filtering logic.

  • Official documentation: Access control and permissions in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

q129.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains a lakehouse.

You have a Microsoft Entra tenant that contains a user named User1.

You need to ensure that User1 can create items in Workspace1. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

Which workspace role should you assign to User1?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Contributor

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option B: ContributorWhy it is correct: The requirement in the question states that User1 must be able to create items in the workspace and that the solution must strictly follow the principle of least privilege. Within the Microsoft Fabric permission model, the Contributor role grants all the permissions needed to create, edit, delete and publish items (such as notebooks, warehouses, lakehouses and reports) within the workspace. At the same time, it restricts advanced administrative tasks and access management, so it represents the lowest possible privilege level that allows content creation.

  • Official documentation: Roles in Microsoft Fabric workspaces - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option D: Viewer (Viewer)Why it is incorrect: The Viewer role grants view-only read rights over the existing items in the workspace. It does not allow creating, modifying or deleting any new item, so it does not meet the user's main requirement.

  • Official documentation: Viewer role capabilities in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option A: Member (Member)Why it is incorrect: Although a Member can create and edit items, this role also grants the privilege to add new users to the workspace and manage other role assignments. Granting user management permissions when the requirement only calls for creating items directly violates the principle of least privilege.

  • Official documentation: Member vs. Contributor role privileges - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Admin (Admin)Why it is incorrect: The Admin role grants full and absolute control over the entire workspace, including the ability to delete the whole workspace, reassign capacities and manage all security settings. It is the highest privilege level, which completely violates the principle of least privilege required in the scenario.

  • Official documentation: Scope of the Admin role in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Note: This question is part of a series of questions that present the same scenario. Each question in the series contains a unique solution that might meet the stated goals. Some question sets might have more than one correct solution, while others might not have a correct solution.

You have an Azure key vault named KeyVault1 that contains secrets.

You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1. Workspace contains a notebook named Notebook1 that performs the following tasks:

• Loads stage data to the target tables in a lakehouse

• Triggers the refresh of a semantic model

You plan to add functionality to Notebook1 that will use the Fabric API to monitor the semantic model refreshes.

You need to retrieve the registered application ID and secret from KeyVault1 to generate the authentication token.

Solution: You use the following code segment:

Use notebookutils.credentials.putSecret and specify the key vault URL and the name of a linked service.

Does this meet the goal?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: No

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option B: No Why the answer is correct (It does not meet the goal): The main objective of the scenario is to retrieve (read) an application ID and a secret already stored in an Azure Key Vault instance (KeyVault1) in order to use them for authentication.

The function described in the proposed solution, notebookutils.credentials.putSecret, has a completely opposite purpose: it is used to store or write a new secret value inside an Azure Key Vault. Trying to use putSecret to read credentials will cause a syntax or parameter error, since this method requires you to provide a secret value to save (secretValue). To retrieve existing secrets from the Key Vault within a Fabric notebook, the correct function to use is notebookutils.credentials.getSecret(akvName, secret). Therefore, the described solution does not meet the stated goal.

answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect option

Option A: Yes Why it is incorrect: Marking that "Yes" meets the goal is false, since it rests on the conceptual error of confusing write methods (putSecret) with read methods (getSecret). Using a function aimed at writing or saving data instead of extracting it completely breaks the logic of the authentication code needed to connect to the Fabric API.

q131.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that uses version control.

Workspace1 and Azure DevOps are integrated.

In Azure DevOps, developers create a branch named Branch1 to test extract, transform, and load (ETL) updates.

You need to connect Workspace1 to Branch1. The solution must ensure that all the existing content in Branch1 is available in Workspace1.

What should you do?
options: From Workspace1, select Source control, and then select Sync.
From Workspace1, select Source control, select Current branch, select Branch1, and then select Commit.
From Azure DevOps, merge the contents of the main branch into Branch1.
From Workspace1, select Source control, and then select Branch out to new workspace.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: From Workspace1, select Source control, select Current branch, select Branch1, and then select Commit.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option B: From Workspace1, select Source control, select Current branch, select Branch1, and then select Commit. Why it is correct: In Azure DevOps version control integration within Microsoft Fabric, a workspace is connected by default to a main branch (for example, main or master). When developers work on a specific feature or test branch (such as Branch1) and you need all the existing content in that branch to be available in the workspace, you must change the active target branch in the Fabric source control settings pane. To do this, you select the source control option, expand the Current branch selection, choose Branch1 from the list and proceed to commit or sync the connection so that the content of that branch is loaded into the workspace.

  • Official documentation: Connecting a workspace to an Azure DevOps repository and switching branches - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: From Workspace1, select Source control, and then select Sync. Why it is incorrect: The Sync action synchronizes changes bidirectionally between the workspace and the branch that is already connected at the moment. If the workspace is still linked to the default main branch, selecting sync will bring in the changes from main, but it will not automatically switch the workspace to point to and pull the content of Branch1.

  • Official documentation: Syncing a workspace with Git - Microsoft Learn

Option C: From Azure DevOps, merge the contents of the main branch into Branch1. Why it is incorrect: Merging the main branch into Branch1 changes the code in Azure DevOps, but it does not solve the problem of linking the Fabric workspace to Branch1. The Fabric environment would keep pointing to the main repository without knowing that it must switch its operating context to the new branch.

  • Official documentation: Managing branches and merges in Azure DevOps - Microsoft Learn

Option D: From Workspace1, select Source control, and then select Branch out to new workspace. Why it is incorrect: This option does not exist in the native Git management interface in Fabric. A workspace is not "branched out" in that way to switch branches; the correct way to point to another development branch is to change the current branch in the source control settings of the existing workspace.

  • Official documentation: Source control settings in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

You have a Fabric workspace.

You plan to deploy two Apache Spark environments that will each contain one of the following notebooks:

• Notebook1: A data ingestion notebook that will run as a scheduled Spark job • Notebook2: An ad hoc notebook for interactive data analysis that will be used by a team of analysts and data scientists

You need to configure the Spark environments to meet the following requirements:

• For the environment that contains Notebook1, minimize compute costs.

• For the environment that contains Notebook2, support multiple concurrent users.

What should you use for each environment? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Notebook1: A serverless Spark environment

  • Notebook2: A custom Spark pool that has multiple nodes

Detailed analysis of the correct options

Environment for Notebook1: A serverless Spark environment

  • Why it is correct: For a scheduled ingestion notebook that runs periodically (such as a batch job), using a serverless Spark environment or autoscale billing optimizes costs to the maximum. Under this model, the system eliminates the cost of idle resources and bills strictly for the active run time of the Spark job, which aligns perfectly with the need to minimize costs in non-continuous scheduled workloads.

  • Official documentation: Apache Spark capacity management and billing in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Environment for Notebook2: A custom Spark pool that has multiple nodes

  • Why it is correct: For ad hoc interactive analysis performed by a whole team of analysts and data scientists, a dedicated and robust infrastructure is required that can support concurrency and the distribution of heavy tasks in parallel. A custom Spark pool (cluster) configured with multiple nodes provides the performance and horizontal scalability needed to avoid resource contention among the many concurrent users.

  • Official documentation: Apache Spark compute overview in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

For the Notebook1 environment (discarded options):

  • A custom Spark pool that has multiple nodes and high concurrency mode enabled / A custom Spark pool that has a single small node and high concurrency mode enabled: Configuring multiple nodes or small nodes with high concurrency in a scheduled ingestion job introduces maintenance overhead or scale limitations that do not optimize the cost minimization of on-demand infrastructure.

  • A starter pool: Although starter pools offer fast start-up times, they are not designed for the cost-minimization model at the scale of heavy scheduled jobs compared with Fabric's flexible serverless compute.

  • Official documentation: Spark cost and performance optimization in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

For the Notebook2 environment (discarded options):

  • A custom Spark pool that has a single small node: A single small node would immediately collapse under the concurrent workload of multiple analysts and data scientists running heavy ad hoc queries.

  • A serverless Spark environment / A starter pool: For high-demand, multi-user, ad hoc interactive collaborative environments, relying solely on ephemeral environments without the consistency of custom multiple nodes can cause latency and bottlenecks in interactive sessions.

  • Official documentation: Capacity planning and Spark clusters - Microsoft Learn

q133.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1.

You perform the following actions:

• Connect Workspace1 to a Git repository and select the main branch.

• Create a new branch named feature1 and modify Lakehouse1.

• Merge the changes from feature1 into the main branch.

You need to ensure that the changes are available in Workspace1. The solution must minimize changes to Workspace1.

What should you do?
options: Disconnect Workspace1 from the Git repository and reconnect Workspace1 to the main branch.
From Workspace1, select Source control, and then select Updates.
From Workspace1, select Source control, and then select Commit.
Switch Workspace1 to the feature1 branch and refresh the workspace.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: From Workspace1, select Source control, and then select Updates.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option B: From Workspace1, select Source control, and then select Updates. Why it is correct: In Git version control integration in Microsoft Fabric, when changes are made in a development branch (such as feature1) and are merged remotely in the repository into the main branch (main), the workspace linked to that main branch will detect that the state of the remote repository is ahead of the current state of the workspace. To reflect these new changes cleanly and directly without altering the environment configuration, you open the workspace's Source control panel and select the option to update or sync the changes coming from Git. This action downloads and applies the lakehouse changes in the workspace, minimizing manual actions entirely.

  • Official documentation: Branch management and synchronization in Fabric Git integration - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: Disconnect Workspace1 from the Git repository and reconnect Workspace1 to the main branch. Why it is incorrect: Disconnecting and reconnecting the workspace is a disruptive and unnecessary operation that breaks the lifecycle link and does not meet the requirement to minimize changes to the workspace, in addition to introducing risks of item metadata inconsistency.

  • Official documentation: Connecting and disconnecting Git repositories in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option C: From Workspace1, select Source control, and then select Commit. Why it is incorrect: The Commit action is used exclusively to package and send local changes made within the workspace to the Git repository. In this scenario, the changes were already applied and merged in the remote repository, so committing from the workspace will not bring the updates down.

  • Official documentation: Committing changes in Git integration - Microsoft Learn

Option D: Switch Workspace1 to the feature1 branch and refresh the workspace. Why it is incorrect: Switching the workspace to the feature1 branch is a logical error, since the development cycle for that feature has already finished and its changes were already formally merged into the main branch. The working environment must remain linked to the main branch to reflect the stable, up-to-date version of the project.

  • Official documentation: Git development workflow in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

q134.stem:
You have an Azure subscription that contains a blob storage account named sa1. sa1 contains two files named File1.csv and File2.csv.

You have a Fabric tenant that contains the items shown in the following table.

You need to configure Pipeline1 to perform the following actions:

• At 2 PM each day, process File1.csv and load the file into flh1.

• At 5 PM each day, process File2.csv and load the file into flh1.

The solution must minimize development effort.

What should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: A data pipeline schedule

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option: A data pipeline schedule Why it is correct: In Microsoft Fabric, the native, built-in mechanism for running pipelines on a recurring, clock-based basis is the scheduling feature (Schedule). The schedule interface lets you add multiple specific times (such as 14:00 and 17:00) within the same configuration. To meet the strict requirement of minimizing development effort, you should use this single pipeline (Pipeline1) with a single schedule, and inside the pipeline use a dynamic expression (evaluating the system time) that decides whether the file to copy is File1.csv or File2.csv. This avoids having to create duplicates of the pipeline or provision new items in the workspace. Official documentation: Scheduling data pipelines in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option: A data pipeline trigger Why it is incorrect: Unlike the older Azure Data Factory nomenclature, in the Microsoft Fabric architecture, runs based purely on clock time are managed in the Schedule section. The term trigger is reserved in the Fabric interface for runs based on infrastructure events, such as the storage events trigger that reacts to the physical creation of a file (BlobCreated) in OneLake. Official documentation: Storage event triggers in pipelines - Microsoft Learn

Option: An activator Why it is incorrect: Activator is a Real-Time Intelligence item designed to evaluate logical conditions or business changes in the data (for example, if sales drop in a Power BI report) and generate alerts. It is not a cron-style time orchestrator for batch pipelines. It would also require creating a new item in the workspace, configuring it and linking it, which maximizes development effort and violates the business requirement. Official documentation: Introduction to Activator in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option: A job definition Why it is incorrect: A Spark job definition is a Fabric item designed exclusively to package, configure and run pure Apache Spark code (such as Python or Scala scripts or JAR files). The question explicitly requires configuring Pipeline1, which is an orchestrating data pipeline, not a Spark code execution job. Official documentation: What is an Apache Spark job definition - Microsoft Learn

q135.stem:

-

You have a Fabric workspace that contains a large table named Table1. Table1 contains 2 billion rows.

You have a data source that generates a data file every 30 minutes. The file contains only changes that occurred since the last file was generated.

You plan to deploy a data pipeline that will process each data file when it is generated and load the contents into Table1.

You need to recommend which loading pattern to use for the following operations:

• Create new records.

• Delete existing records.

The solution must support the versioning of existing records.

What should you recommend for each operation? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Create new records: Incremental

  • Deleted existing records: Snapshot

Detailed analysis of the correct options

Create new records: Incremental

  • Why it is correct: Since the data source generates a file every 30 minutes containing exclusively the recent changes and the table has 2 billion rows, an incremental load pattern lets you efficiently append the new records directly to the table without having to reload or scan the entire massive table every half hour.

  • Official documentation: Incremental data load patterns in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Deleted existing records: Snapshot

  • Why it is correct: The requirement explicitly demands supporting versioning of existing records and handling deletions. With an incremental flow based purely on recent changes, only added or modified records are visible, making it hard to directly detect which data was deleted at the source. A snapshot approach, or snapshot-based state tracking, captures the full state at a point in time, making it easier to compare states to identify the deleted records and preserve the historical versions prior to deletion.

  • Official documentation: Versioning and change management strategies in Delta Lake - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Full (full load):

  • Why it is incorrect: Applying a full load pattern every 30 minutes on a massive table of 2 billion rows is highly inefficient, generates a disproportionate consumption of compute and capacity resources, and violates architecture best practices for data sources that already provide change-based incremental flows.

  • Official documentation: Performance considerations for bulk data ingestion in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Incremental for deleting records:

  • Why it is incorrect: A purely incremental pattern over files that only contain inserts or updates does not natively include explicit deletion metadata or records, so by itself it cannot reliably track deleted records while maintaining the required historical versioning.

  • Official documentation: Design patterns for data synchronization and deletions - Microsoft Learn

q136.stem:
You have a Fabric lakehouse that contains the resources shown in the following table.

You need to use a notebook to query for customers in the United States and load the filtered data into USCustomers. The solution must minimize the number of scripts used.

Which statement should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: customers.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").saveAsTable("USCustomers")

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option C: customers.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").saveAsTable("USCustomers") Why it is correct: In a Microsoft Fabric lakehouse, the native and default format for managed tables is Delta Lake (format("delta")). When running a customer filtering process to update or populate the destination table (USCustomers), you must use overwrite mode (mode("overwrite")) to ensure the table cleanly reflects the current filtered dataset without duplicating rows accumulated across successive runs. Likewise, using the .saveAsTable("USCustomers") method lets you save the DataFrame directly as a managed table in the lakehouse with the minimum code effort and without having to specify complex physical file paths, meeting the requirement to minimize the number of scripts and commands used.

  • Official documentation: Writing data to Delta Lake in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: customers.write.format("parquet").mode("append").saveAsTable("USCustomers") Why it is incorrect: It uses the flat Parquet file format instead of the Delta Lake format, which is required to take advantage of the transactional and table optimization features in the Fabric lakehouse. It also uses append mode, which would cause successive runs to accumulate and duplicate customer records instead of maintaining a clean snapshot of the filtered United States customers.

  • Official documentation: Considerations on Delta vs. Parquet table formats - Microsoft Learn

Option B: customers.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save("Tables/USCustomers") Why it is incorrect: Although it correctly uses the Delta Lake format and overwrite mode, it uses the .save("Tables/USCustomers") method pointing directly to the file path instead of .saveAsTable(). This writes the data as a set of files without properly registering them as a first-class managed table in the lakehouse catalog, which would require additional scripts to formally create the table.

  • Official documentation: Difference between save and saveAsTable methods in Apache Spark - Microsoft Learn

Option D: customers.write.format("parquet").mode("append").save("Tables/USCustomers") Why it is incorrect: It combines multiple critical errors: it specifies the Parquet format instead of Delta, it uses append mode, which duplicates the data on each run, and it saves the data as files in a generic path instead of registering a managed table, failing both the lakehouse architecture and the goal of minimizing scripts.

  • Official documentation: Best practices for data persistence in a lakehouse - Microsoft Learn

q137.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1, a Dataflow Gen2 named Dataflow1, and a pipeline named Pipeline1. Dataflow1 loads data into Lakehouse1.

You need to ensure that Dataflow1 always performs a full data load into Lakehouse1. The solution must minimize how long it takes to load the data.

What should you do?
options: For Dataflow1, set Update method to Replace.
To Dataflow1, add a data preview.
To Pipeline1, add an activity to invoke a SQL script.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: For Dataflow1, set Update method to Replace.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option B: For Dataflow1, set Update method to Replace. Why it is correct: In Microsoft Fabric, when a Dataflow Gen2 is used to write data to a destination such as a lakehouse (Lakehouse1), the destination table settings let you define the Update method. Setting this option to Replace tells the Power Query engine that on each run it must empty the destination table and load the full dataset from scratch. This natively guarantees that the table always keeps an up-to-date full load with the minimum processing time, since it avoids the need to write custom cleanup scripts or complex change-tracking logic.

  • Official documentation: Configuring destination options in Microsoft Fabric Dataflow Gen2 - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: Change the pipeline templates. Why it is incorrect: Pipeline templates are predefined structures used to speed up the initial creation of new reusable workflows. Modifying a template has no effect on the load behavior or the internal refresh logic of a Dataflow Gen2 that is already deployed.

  • Official documentation: Using pipeline templates in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option C: To Dataflow1, add a data preview. Why it is incorrect: The data preview feature in Power Query is an interactive design and debugging tool aimed at development. It is used exclusively to inspect the first rows while building the transformations in the user interface, so it has no impact on the performance or on the execution of the full load in production.

  • Official documentation: Previewing data in Dataflow Gen2 - Microsoft Learn

Option D: To Pipeline1, add an activity to invoke a SQL script. Why it is incorrect: Adding a SQL script activity in the pipeline to manually truncate or manipulate the table before or after running the dataflow introduces an unnecessary layer of complexity, increases the total development time and duplicates the orchestration processes, when the Dataflow Gen2 itself natively handles overwriting and replacing the data in an optimized way.

  • Official documentation: Script activity in Fabric data pipelines - Microsoft Learn
