q138.stem:
HOTSPOT

-

You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains an Azure Data Factory pipeline named Pipeline1.

You need to monitor the execution and activity status of Pipeline1 and automatically email an alert if the pipeline fails. The solution must minimize development and administrative effort.

What should you use to monitor Pipeline1, and what should you use to email the alert? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Monitor Pipeline1: Monitor hub

  • Email alert: A Microsoft Power Automate flow

Detailed analysis of the correct options

Monitor Pipeline1: Monitor hub

  • Why it is correct: The Microsoft Fabric monitor hub is the native, centralized tool designed specifically to track, audit the run status of and review the activities of workspace items (including pipelines) with minimal administrative effort, without needing to configure external dashboards or additional diagnostic infrastructure.

  • Official documentation: Monitor hub in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Email alert: A Microsoft Power Automate flow

  • Why it is correct: To send automated email alerts when a pipeline fails while minimizing development effort and leveraging the native integration ecosystem, you use a Microsoft Power Automate flow. Fabric data pipelines integrate seamlessly with Power Automate through activities or actions based on error conditions (Failure / On failure), making it possible to trigger email notifications simply and directly.

  • Official documentation: Using Power Automate with data pipelines in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

For Monitor Pipeline1:

  • Azure Monitor: It is a solution oriented to Azure infrastructure and global resources. Although Fabric emits certain logs to Azure, for direct internal monitoring of item runs within the native Fabric service interface, the standard and direct component is the monitor hub.

  • Real-Time Intelligence monitoring: It is focused on monitoring streaming events and real-time Kusto databases, not on batch operational tracking of data pipelines.

  • Official documentation: Monitoring data pipelines in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

For Email alert:

  • A Web activity: It requires programming manual HTTP calls through webhooks against external messaging services or email APIs, which needlessly increases development effort compared with a native automated solution.

  • A Fabric Activator action: Activator is designed to watch metrics and real-time data streams to generate alerts or automated actions on continuous streams, not to manage traditional failure notifications for batch pipelines.

  • A Data Factory trigger: Triggers manage when pipelines start or run (by events or schedules), but they do not have the intrinsic ability to compose and send alert emails on failures.

  • Official documentation: Failure actions and conditions in Fabric pipelines - Microsoft Learn

q139.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a data pipeline named Pipeline1 and a notebook named Notebook1. Pipeline1 contains an activity that is used to run Notebook1. Pipeline1 is scheduled to run every 10 minutes.

You receive an alert that Pipeline1 failed during the notebook execution activity.

You need to identify in which cell the failure occurred.

What should you do from Monitor in the Fabric admin center?
options: Select the entry for the notebook execution, and then select the logs.
Select the entry for the notebook execution, and then view the item snapshot.
Select the entry for the pipeline execution, and then view the activity run.
Select the entry for the pipeline execution, and then select the output.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Select the entry for the notebook execution, and then view the item snapshot.

Detailed analysis of the correct option

Option B: Select the entry for the notebook execution, and then view the item snapshot.

  • Why it is correct: When a pipeline runs a notebook and a failure occurs, the monitor hub lets you drill into the specific details of the notebook run. By selecting the entry for the notebook run and opening the item snapshots tab, you can examine the read-only code of the notebook as it was at the time of the run, showing the state of each cell in order and pointing out exactly which cell caused the error.

  • Official documentation: Detailed monitoring of Apache Spark applications in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Detailed analysis of the incorrect options

Option A: Select the entry for the notebook execution, and then select the logs.

  • Why it is incorrect: The driver logs or Spark process logs are useful for diagnosing general infrastructure problems, but they do not present the cell-by-cell structure of the notebook that would let you visually identify the exact failure in the code directly.

  • Official documentation: Fabric notebook troubleshooting guide - Microsoft Learn

Option C: Select the entry for the pipeline execution, and then view the activity run.

  • Why it is incorrect: Inspecting the overall pipeline run and the activity run only confirms that the notebook activity failed at the global orchestration level, but it does not provide the granular, cell-code-level detail within the notebook that is required to identify the exact source of the error.

  • Official documentation: Monitoring data pipelines in Fabric - Microsoft Learn

Option D: Select the entry for the pipeline execution, and then select the output.

  • Why it is incorrect: The output of the activity within the pipeline shows the returned parameters or the generic error message returned by the service, but it lacks the cell-by-cell view that the notebook snapshot offers.

  • Official documentation: Notebook activity overview in Fabric - Microsoft Learn
